A Hyperliquid whale holds a $44 million long on 35 million XRP, nearly 80% of large-wallet XRP longs, with liquidation at $0.9626, about 23% below the current price.

Crypto liquidations reached $386.42 million in 24 hours, 88% of them longs, led by Bitcoin ($100.74 million) and Ethereum ($49.31 million).

US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $398.62 million in net daily outflows, led by Fidelity’s FBTC ($164 million), while 44,857 ETH left spot Ethereum ETFs.

Binance posted a record $15.4 billion weekly net outflow following a $6.3 billion hack the FBI attributed to North Korea.

This week’s key US triggers are the midterm elections and JOLTS (Tuesday), ISM services (Wednesday), the Fed balance sheet (Thursday) and Nonfarm Payrolls (Friday).

The crypto market greeted Tuesday morning, November 3, with a massive wave of margin position closures. Over the past 24 hours, the positions of 94,997 traders were forcibly liquidated for a total of $386.42 million, with 88% of all losses ($339.92 million) falling on long contracts, while Bitcoin ($100.74 million) and Ethereum ($49.31 million) led in liquidation volume as per CoinGlass.

A strong bearish skew persists in the US spot ETF sector: the net daily outflow from BTC funds amounted to $398.62 million, with the main blow falling on the Fidelity fund (FBTC), which saw $164 million leave. Over the day, 44,857 ETH were withdrawn from spot Ethereum ETFs. The combined assets under management (AUM) of all crypto ETFs stand at $95.83 billion as per SoSoValue.

The current daily outflow has spread across the entire line of exchange-traded products: SOL funds lost 129.19 thousand coins, outflows from XRP products amounted to 128.54 thousand tokens, and the specialized HYPE and ZEC funds shed 85.07 thousand and 13.53 thousand coins, respectively. Major operators are preemptively pulling liquidity out of volatile instruments ahead of the US midterm elections.

Amid the decline in market capitalization, a sharp split among participants has emerged: while retail investors are locking in losses en masse and most whales are betting on a decline, some large on-chain operators are opening aggressive counter-trend positions on decentralized exchanges.

The main event of the morning session was the actions of an unknown major player on the Hyperliquid platform, who, despite the overall market decline (NEAR dropped to $3.79, BNB to $697.67), stubbornly holds an XRP long worth tens of millions of dollars, turning the contract into the main barometer of local altcoin resilience.

The decentralized futures platform Hyperliquid is currently accumulating peak institutional volumes. At the same time, on-chain analytics of top wallets with balances of $1 million or more shows a strong bearish skew in open interest.

Of these wallets' total open positions of $4.5 billion, short contracts (shorts) account for $3.08 billion. Their long volume is limited to a modest $1.46 billion.

Leviathan addresses with positions of $50 million or more are almost unanimously betting on a further market decline. Against this grim backdrop, the long position of wallet '0x31b1ecf848443472e34d204a134812d86ab01434' remains the largest and riskiest counter-trend position in the system.

The whale holds 35.03 million XRP tokens. The notional value of the open position is $44.05 million at 10x Cross leverage.

The average entry price is $1.1298. At the peak of the morning momentum, the whale's unrealized profit exceeded $4.47 million, which amounts to more than 101% net return on the margin capital invested.

At the same time, the account's overall result is far from ideal: due to overall asset volatility, this wallet's net PnL over the past 30 days has fallen by $8.45 million.

The critical threshold in this whole story remains the forced liquidation price. The automatic position closure threshold sits at $0.9626.

The current XRP market price of around $1.2558 leaves the trader a buffer of about 23% to the liquidation point.

Large wallets' XRP positions on Hyperliquid are also skewed toward the bears. Against long positions of $55.70 million stands a massive wall of shorts worth $80.93 million. Nearly 80% of these longs belong to a single whale.

This morning's news backdrop points to a massive and painful restructuring of the entire market infrastructure. The central theme remains a severe liquidity crisis on centralized exchanges.

$6.3 billion Binance hack and the FBI's position: The agency officially attributed the attack to North Korean state cyber units. An analysis by lawyers at Reed Smith and Lathrop GPM showed that the exchange's insurance policies will not cover the damage. Standard D&O insurance protects only top management, while war exclusion clauses fully rule out payouts in the event of cyberwarfare waged by foreign states.

Record outflow of $15.4 billion: The weekly net capital outflow from Binance hit an all-time high. This volume exceeds the individual reserves of Bybit or Bitfinex and surpasses the combined balance of Gate, Bitget and KuCoin, which keeps the price of BNB at local lows.

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao's loud statements about rising risks to the financial system from automated AI-powered cyberattacks came amid the incident at the exchange he created, which showed the ineffectiveness of classic defense mechanisms against coordinated cyber operations. Zhao stressed that commercial banks, due to outdated IT architecture, are more vulnerable than crypto platforms.

Against this backdrop, decentralized protocols are confidently expanding their institutional presence. Hyperliquid's annual revenue has reached $713 million, and trading volume in perpetuals on stocks and commodities via HIP-3 has exceeded $500 billion. Building on these technologies, the operator of the New York Stock Exchange (ICE) and Kraken are already preparing to launch regulated futures in the US with White House support.

Meanwhile, serious changes are also taking place at the level of the largest L1 ecosystems. House of Stake (NEAR Protocol) participants approved the deflationary initiative HSP-029 with 99.96% of the vote, reducing annual emissions from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. Daily issuance of new tokens is being cut from 89,500 to 57,300, while amid the general market decline the asset briefly dropped to $3.79.

Skepticism is meanwhile growing in the Ripple camp: the company reports that issuance of its dollar token RLUSD has surpassed $1 billion through partnerships with trust banks, but XRP holders are voicing open dissatisfaction. RLUSD is a centralized asset subject to freezing under US law, while XRP's decentralized status is not yet reflected in its market valuation.

At the same time, the Ethereum Foundation launched a platform for using the network as digital public infrastructure (DPI) for governments. Case studies on digital identity in Bhutan and confidential humanitarian aid systems have been published. At Devcon 8 in Mumbai, Vitalik Buterin called for developing verifiable code to minimize dependence on closed software and AI systems.

In the coming sessions, capital flows in the crypto market will be largely determined by external macroeconomic and political triggers. Investors and market makers need to keep the following critical factors in focus:

US Congressional midterm elections: The main political factor of this Tuesday, forcing large funds to preemptively close margin positions, cut leverage and hedge risks ahead of a change in the regulatory landscape.

Official JOLTS labor market report: Tuesday's release of job openings data will determine the short-term dynamics of the US dollar index and directly affect liquidity in high-risk assets.

ISM non-manufacturing business activity indices: Wednesday's statistics will highlight the real state of the US economy and shape the medium-term sentiment of major futures market operators.

Fed balance sheet on Thursday and Friday's Nonfarm Payrolls report: The key macroeconomic triggers of the week, which will lock in the final direction of capital flows through the end of the month.

#5253. XRP Whales Reach Highest Supply Share in 4 Years; Can Price Reclaim $3 Level?

XRP recovered slightly by Tuesday’s close after falling the day before, trading near $1.31 as traders assessed fresh signs of whale accumulation amid lingering selling pressure.

In a Tuesday post on X, Santiment reported that wallets holding at least 10 million XRP now control 46.87 billion tokens, about 68.5% of the cryptocurrency’s supply. That marks the largest share this group has held since November 2022.

“The key signal is that these massive holders have kept increasing exposure even while XRP struggles near $1.29,” Santiment wrote, suggesting that large investors remain willing to accumulate despite the token’s weakness.

The figures mark a shift from an earlier warning by analyst Ali Martinez, who cited a decline in wallets holding between 10 million and 100 million XRP, from 351 to 339 since November 2022. He also noted that exchange balances rose from 11.003 billion to about 11.05 billion XRP, which could partly explain the ongoing price stagnation. Martinez warned that continued selling by large holders could send XRP toward $0.98.

However, Santiment’s latest figures suggest that accumulation among the largest wallets may be strengthening even as the price struggles.

“Large stakeholders accumulating through weakness suggests conviction remains strong beneath the price action,” Santiment stated.

The analytics platform identified $1.30 as the immediate pivot, with $1.90 as a stronger level to confirm a potential recovery.

Meanwhile, CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost reported a sharp drop in XRP derivatives exposure, potentially easing some of the pressure from leveraged positions. According to him, Binance open interest fell to $445 million, below its 180-day average of approximately $460 million.

Since September 22, the metric has declined nearly 28%, while XRP’s price has dropped 17% over the same period. He attributed the decline partly to falling prices, which reduce the value of outstanding positions, and to liquidations triggered during the sell-off.

“This deleveraging dynamic is a rather positive signal as it suggests that pressure on XRP futures is gradually easing,” the analyst said.

Moreover, Darkfost cited previous episodes in which falling open interest preceded substantial XRP rallies, suggesting a similar scenario could unfold.

“We saw this in mid-September, when XRP gained 32% in the following period, and after the mid-August episode, which was followed by a 72% rally.” He added.

Martinez also identified a potential technical catalyst for a rebound. The analyst said the TD Sequential indicator had flashed a buy signal on XRP’s three-day chart, noting that the previous three comparable signals preceded rebounds of 31%, 24% and 18%. However, the setup depends on XRP holding its support level.

“Hold it, and XRP could rebound toward $1.40. Lose it while whales continue taking profits, and $0.98 could be next,” Martinez said.

Elsewhere, analyst Joep Gerla highlighted XRP’s prolonged consolidation as a possible precursor to a larger advance. He compared the current price structure with previous consolidation periods that preceded rallies of 63,617% in 2017–2018, 1,687% in 2020–2021 and 901% in 2024–2025.

“XRP has been in prolonged consolidation, a structure that has preceded major expansion phases in previous cycles,” Gerla wrote. “The edge goes to those who stay patient before the breakout.”

At press time, XRP was trading at $1.31, up 2.13% in the past 24 hours.

According to popular Cardano explorer Cexplorer there are over 131 million ADA currently delegated to retired stake pools, leaving thousands of delegators without staking rewards.

Cardano staking pools offer ADA holders a way to passively earn rewards for securing the blockchain by delegating their coins to network validators, all without locking up or losing control of their funds.

Cexplorer recently posted on X that 59,025 delegators still have their ADA delegated to pools that have retired. Therefore, they are not earning staking rewards on their current delegations.

⚠️ Over 131M $ADA is currently delegated to retired stake pools. 59,025 delegators staking with those pools are not earning any staking rewards. If you're one of them, consider choosing a new stake pool to keep earning rewards and supporting Cardano's decentralization. https://t.co/L9mitriW2P

According to Cexplorer data, 131.63 million ADA is still delegated to retired pools and the number of retired pools is given as 2,720. Holders can delegate ADA to a stake pool and earn rewards as long as the pool they choose is active, which contributes to network security and decentralization.

However, when a stake pool retires, delegators must select another active pool if they want to continue earning rewards. Their ADA does not disappear simply because the pool has retired, but the delegation no longer provides the expected staking benefits.

Users who are delegating their ADA to such retired pools are urged to review their staking arrangements and consider moving their ADA to active stake pools.

Major crypto exchange Binance has commenced phased withdrawals for crypto networks days after it suffered a hack that impacted nearly $6.3 billion in client assets. In line with this, Binance will reopen withdrawals for Cardano (ADA) on the BSC network beginning at 04:00 (UTC) on November 3, 2026.

In Dijkstra upgrade news, Node 11.2 is out as a pre-release. It carries the full Dijkstra hard fork feature set apart from Leios and will move DijkstraNet into the Dijkstra era so downstream teams can start integration testing.

Node 11.3 includes Leios and is set to deliver the complete Dijkstra feature set. A tagged pre-release is realistically three to four weeks away, two at the earliest.

While the recent purchase has brought the company's total holdings to 849,327 BTC, worth about $65.9 billion, up from the 848,516 BTC it held the previous week, Strategy's Bitcoin holdings are rapidly expanding.

Although Bitcoin's price action has remained weak, it is still trading above the average purchase price of each Bitcoin owned by Strategy at over $77,000. As such, the company has been able to generate substantial unrealized profits of over $919 million as of November 3.

While Strategy has continued to win on its relentless Bitcoin bets even at a time when the market is facing extreme volatility, market watchers are already asking the bigger question about how much gain the company could secure if Bitcoin eventually recovers this month.

With Strategy already sitting on over $919 million in profit when Bitcoin is trading around $77,000, the firm is poised to hit multi-billion profits later this month if Bitcoin reclaims support around $80,000.

#5249. Hyperliquid (HYPE) Rallies as CFTC Approves First-Ever US Stock Perpetuals

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Hyperliquid’s native token (HYPE) responded with confident growth to the historic decision of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), which for the first time allowed trading of perpetual futures on individual stocks (Equity Perpetuals).

The regulatory shift de facto legitimizes a product that developed predominantly in DeFi ecosystems and opens the way for the institutional expansion of Hyperliquid’s infrastructure, which served as the trigger for the asset’s rally.

According to the CFTC release of November 3, 2026, equity perpetual contracts received the status of security futures under joint CFTC and SEC oversight, with the possibility of trading on dual-registered exchanges.

Today, equity perps can begin trading for the first time on @CFTC registered exchanges. This move reflects my commitment to ensuring that America’s markets remain the most innovative, liquid, and well-regulated in the world. Instead of being forced to turn to offshore, unregulated venues to access equity perpetual futures, Americans may now access equity perps on CFTC-regulated markets subject to robust safeguards. I appreciate the continued partnership of @SECGov and @SECPaulSAtkins as we work to further harmonize our agencies' regulatory initiatives.

The agency’s goal is to bring back into the U.S. legal field billions in volume that had been flowing to offshore crypto platforms. The instrument is being launched under the Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000 (CFMA), which eliminates the need to pass new laws.

The regulator’s pragmatic step directly boosts Hyperliquid’s capitalization. Through its HIP-3 framework (in particular, the trade[XYZ] platform), the project already controls the largest on-chain market for perps on Apple, Nvidia and Tesla, with daily turnover in the hundreds of millions of dollars.

The new CFTC classification fully matched the structure that the Hyperliquid Policy Center advocated in official submissions to the authorities.

Now financial giant ICE (owner of the NYSE), which previously invested in trade[XYZ], gets a legal basis for creating a regulated American platform on Hyperliquid technology, while Payward (Kraken’s parent company) is accelerating the launch of a similar product through the regulated exchange Bitnomial.

Despite legalization in the U.S., Hyperliquid maintains a strict geoblock for American residents, continuing to serve the global market thanks to its key trump cards: on-chain liquidity, 24/7 trading and flexible margin conditions.

Local exchanges in the U.S. will inevitably face the limitations of traditional Wall Street sessions and strict SEC leverage limits in the early stages.

This moves Hyperliquid from the status of an offshore experiment into the role of the main technology donor of the American financial market, with the possibility of monetizing its infrastructure through fee opportunities from the trades of regulated partners.

The market instantly priced these prospects into the asset’s value. TradingView charts recorded a vertical surge in the HYPE/USD pair immediately after the release was published at 14:02 UTC: the price impulsively broke out of the $84.9-$85.30 corridor tested a local high above $87.40 and consolidated around $86.83, holding a net gain of more than 2%.

ApeCoin didn’t start as just another token; it launched as the economic layer of one of the most recognizable NFT brands in crypto.

Backed by Bored Ape Yacht Club (BAYC) and Yuga Labs, APE surged immediately after launch, briefly capturing the imagination of the entire NFT market. The token was meant to power a broader ecosystem, including the Otherside metaverse, gaming experiences, DAO governance, and Web3 culture initiatives.

But as the NFT market cooled, ApeCoin’s demand followed. The token is now trading near $0.1175, over 84% below its peak, leaving investors questioning whether the ecosystem still has momentum.

So let’s explore CoinPedia’s Ape Price Prediction 2026, 2027 – 2030.

ApeCoin is up 2.03% to $0.117 over the past 24 hours, following an upgrade to ApeChain’s cross-chain infrastructure. On November 4, the official ApeCoin account announced that ApeChain is moving from LayerZero to Chainlink’s Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol (CCIP).

As part of the upgrade, APE and USDC will become Chainlink Cross-Chain Tokens. The change aims to improve security and make it easier to move tokens across chains within the Yuga Labs ecosystem.

APE also gained alongside the broader crypto market. Bitcoin rose 2.77%, while the total crypto market cap increased 2.55%. Reduced uncertainty after the US midterm elections and renewed inflows into US spot Bitcoin ETFs also supported the market.

The future of ApeCoin in the final quarter of 2026 will largely depend on the expansion of the ApeChain ecosystem and the transition to ApeCo. The launch of ApeChain, a dedicated Layer-2 network, introduces a deflationary model where every transaction burns APE used as gas fees, while ApeCo matches 100% of the burned tokens, further reducing the circulating supply.

Another major growth driver is the upcoming official ecosystem launchpad, which aims to fund and support Web3 projects built exclusively on ApeChain.

The transition from ApeCoin DAO to ApeCo is also expected to improve decision-making by replacing community voting with a more structured execution model.

Meanwhile, as Yuga Labs continues developing its metaverse ecosystem, APE is expected to remain the primary currency for trading virtual land, NFTs, avatars, and other digital assets.

ApeCoin (APE) remains in a broader downtrend, with the recent price action showing a long consolidation phase rather than a confirmed reversal. After falling sharply from the $0.70 area, APE has spent several months moving sideways between roughly $0.10 and $0.18.

The token is now trading around $0.1167 and has slipped back toward the lower boundary of this range, making $0.10 a key support zone.

If buyers defend this level and APE rebounds above the range midpoint, the first major resistance is around $0.2419. A sustained breakout above $0.2419 could strengthen the recovery and bring the higher resistance at $0.4821 into focus.

However, a decisive breakdown below $0.10 would weaken the consolidation structure and could lead to further downside.

If ApeChain adoption increases and token unlock pressure disappears, APE could reach $0.4821.

If Otherside launches interactive metaverse experiences and gaming integrations expand, APE could move toward $1.94.

Broader Web3 gaming adoption and NFT ecosystem revival could support APE near $3.21.

By 2029, if ApeChain becomes a dedicated gaming and metaverse hub, APE may approach $7.09.

Long-term ecosystem growth and DAO-driven governance could push APE toward $16.

From CoinPedia’s perspective, ApeCoin’s recovery in 2026 will depend on how quickly ApeChain attracts developers and users beyond the NFT ecosystem.

At the same time, with nearly 90% of the total supply already unlocked, token unlock pressure has largely faded, allowing demand to play a bigger role in price movement.

If ecosystem adoption continues to grow alongside a broader crypto market recovery, CoinPedia forecasts ApeCoin could reach a high of $0.4821 by the end of 2026.

#5247. 99% Cold Wallet Rule Mulled by South Korea Following Binance Hack

South Korean financial regulators are reportedly considering introducing much stricter cryptocurrency storage requirements for local exchanges following the massive $6.3 billion Binance hack.

According to a Nov. 3 report by South Korean news outlet News1, the country’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) is discussing raising the minimum proportion of customer cryptocurrencies that exchanges must store in cold wallets from the current 80% to approximately 99%.

The potential regulatory change comes just days after Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, suffered one of the biggest security breaches in cryptocurrency history.

However, the proposed 99% threshold remains under discussion, and no official decision has been made.

Under South Korea’s existing Virtual Asset User Protection Act, cryptocurrency exchanges are required to store at least 80% of customers’ digital assets in cold wallets.

Unlike hot wallets, which are connected to the internet and used to process everyday transactions, cold wallets are kept offline, making them significantly less vulnerable to remote hacking attacks.

However, the proportion of assets stored offline varies significantly among South Korea’s leading cryptocurrency exchanges.

According to Financial Supervisory Service data cited by local media, Upbit currently has one of the highest cold wallet storage ratios in the country.

As of the end of September, the exchange held approximately 99.17% of customer assets in cold wallets.

Meanwhile, rival cryptocurrency exchange Bithumb stored approximately 94.76% of its assets offline, while Coinone’s cold wallet ratio stood at 85%.

Polkadot (DOT) remains one of the few Layer-0 blockchain networks focused on interoperability. Its architecture allows multiple blockchains to operate together while sharing security.

Recent changes to tokenomics and infrastructure, including Agile Coretime and a supply cap update in March 2026, have altered the network’s economic model. These developments shape expectations for DOT’s price outlook through 2030.

Polkadot is designed as a multi-chain network. It uses a central Relay Chain to connect independent blockchains called parachains.

The introduction of Agile Coretime enables more flexible allocation of network resources. This replaces earlier slot-based systems with an on-demand model.

In late 2025, the price of Polkadot (DOT) experienced significant selling pressure, which continued into H1 2026 and extended into H2 2026.

By August, the price reached a low at the $0.72 support level and staged a mid-month surge. However, after climbing to $1.25 by early September,, it faced sell pressure building around 200-day EMA band. The DOT price showed multiple attempts to break past $1.25 but by late October it ended up retracing back to $0.99-$1.01 area.

If sell pressure continues then it may push the price back down to revisit the $0.72 support level or lower.

However, if the DOT price shows a rise in demand and manages to flip 200-day EMA band, then it could target $2.01. Flipping this level could open the path toward $3.02, with potential to reach $4.70 under stronger bullish momentum.

On October 8, 2026, Following the approval of OpenGov Referendum 1944, Polkadot officially deployed dotUSD on mainnet, which is a protocol-native, decentralized stablecoin governed entirely by the DOT DAO without corporate issuers or centralized points of control.

On July 18, Polkadot highlighted its structural pivot from deep infrastructure development to user-facing applications at the Web3 summit, releasing four technical presentations focused on intuitive product design. The ecosystem is shifting its core focus from building complex background “machinery” toward delivering accessible, consumer-centric software interfaces.

On July 10, at the web3 summit parity technologies shared the details about the event that 190 participants, many of whom had never used Polkadot before, successfully built and deployed their own decentralized applications in under 30 minutes using AI assistance. The hands-on event showcased 272 newly published “.dot” domains and 49 forked applications, proving how simplified infrastructure can dramatically lower the entry barrier for Web3 development.

On July 6, Polkadot have made live the two major staking updates under referenda 1909, and 1910 designed to optimize network security and lower barriers for participants. The dual proposals have introduced self-stake rewards and commission caps for validators and has removed nominator slashing and also slashed unbonding periods for nominators.

On July 5, 2026, the decentralized identity protocol dotID went live as an officially approved username authority for the Polkadot People Chain. Enabled through the successful passage of OpenGov Referendum 1898, the platform follows its massive v2 rollout to issue human-readable “.id” namespaces and automate secure, non-custodial on-chain identity verifications for the entire Polkadot and Kusama ecosystem.

On June 23, Polkadot posted about two new OpenGov referenda 1909 and 1910, that were proposed to overhaul Polkadot’s network security model and optimize overall staking parameter efficiency.

On June 12th Polkadot focussed on centralized communication and highlighted that they are trying to create a decentralized infrastructure to facilitate communication better.

On March 9th, DOT announced that the first Polkadot U.S. ETF, trading as TDOT via 21Shares, has officially launched on the Nasdaq exchange. This milestone provides a regulated investment vehicle for the asset, though investors are encouraged to conduct thorough independent research, as this announcement does not constitute financial advice.

The long-term trajectory of Polkadot price (DOT) reveals a classic “boom and bust” market cycle of massive proportions. Between late 2020 and late 2021, the asset underwent an extraordinary bullish expansion, surging from a low of $1.50 to an all-time high of approximately $56.

This move represented a rally of over 3,500%, establishing a dominant bullish structure on the weekly timeframe. However, the peak in late 2021 marked the beginning of a structural shift, as the market transitioned into a prolonged corrective phase.

The chart shows that the bearish reversal intensified throughout 2022, characterized by the loss of critical psychological and technical support levels at $32 and $24. While a mid-2022 drop to $6.30 was initially perceived by many as a potential market bottom, it wasn’t, and the decline proved more persistent. The downward momentum eventually dragged the price to a low of $3.57 by late 2023.

Despite two notable recovery attempts in early and late 2024, the bulls were unable to reclaim the $12 supply zone, which acted as a heavy ceiling and confirmed the continuation of the macro-downtrend into 2025.

Now, in 2026, all these past occurrences make sense, as by H1 2026 the correction had reached a significant milestone, with DOT touching a new multi-year low of $0.80. Paradoxically, this price action has brought the asset below the “Demand Zone” that ignited the original 2020 bull run.

Currently, DOT/USD appears to have fallen below the green rectangle, which marked a phase of deep accumulation, within a weekly range of $1.35 to $3.57.

Now, in H2, if price sees a rise in demand, it might reenter the accumulation zone above $1.0 and, with the right trigger, may also break past this zone towards a retest of the $12 resistance.

However, in H2, if momentum doesn’t materialize, the price might continue to consolidate or even bleed lower.

However, there is a glimmer of optimism in the latest usage metrics: transaction counts have begun to see a notable uptick in 2026, indicating that while the user base may be smaller, the remaining participants are engaging more deeply with the ecosystem’s growing list of parachains.

A fresh annual report of British company VivoPower PLC, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on November 2, 2026, officially disclosed the parameters of the closure of its cryptocurrency strategy.

The documents recorded the creation and subsequent liquidation of a $5 million stake in the private company Ripple Labs, while also making public the price of their buyback at $300 apiece.

According to the filing, in May 2025, VivoPower announced a large-scale treasury expansion with a target investment volume of up to $100 million in XRP tokens and Ripple Labs equity. In practice, the investments turned out to be more modest: the XRP treasury allocated $5.0 million to the direct acquisition of 41,810 Ripple Labs shares in January 2026.

For institutional investors, buying stakes in the fintech giant itself was a key way to make a large bet on the ecosystem's success.

However, the experiment lasted only nine months from its announcement. As early as February, VivoPower's board of directors decided to fully wind down the crypto direction. Management recognized holding digital assets as less profitable than developing artificial intelligence infrastructure and redirected capital to the purchase of a 41.5 MW data center in Mo i Rana, Norway, for $37.7 million.

The process of liquidating this $5 million stake brought the crypto market an important price insight. In April 2026, Ripple Labs conducted a targeted buyback, taking 882 shares from VivoPower at $300 apiece. The deal brought the British company $264,600 in cash and $159,122 in net profit, giving the community a rare and hard marker of how Ripple's management itself values its business in private trades.

A direct sale of the remaining part of the stake on the open market proved impossible due to the non-public status of the securities. As a result, VivoPower entered into agreements to sell the economic rights to the shares to two South Korean partners, KWeather Co. and Lean Ventures.

As of the filing date, the Korean deals have not yet been legally completed. The remaining 40,928 shares are locked in the Korea Securities Depository (KSD) under a strict one-year lock-up restriction. Due to this freeze and the lack of market liquidity, independent appraisers lowered the book value of this stake to $4.3 million (about $106.16 per share).

The VivoPower story clearly showed the crypto industry the flip side of institutional investments: a direct purchase of stakes in Ripple Labs comes with strict lock-ups and low liquidity, where the only fast source of fiat for exiting the ecosystem is the issuer itself through a private buyback procedure.

Origin Protocol is one of the oldest DeFi projects on Ethereum and has been building in the crypto space for many years. The project focuses on helping users earn passive income through staking and stablecoin products in a simple, flexible way.

Its main products, Origin Ether and Origin Dollar, allow users to earn yield while still keeping control of their funds.

Origin also aims to make DeFi and NFTs easier for more people to use, with the help of its native token, OGN. The project focuses on long-term growth, user rewards, and building a sustainable system.

But many investors are now wondering about one important question: what could be the future price of OGN?

So, let’s explore the Origin Protocol price prediction for 2026, 2027, and 2030.

Origin Protocol is down 1.29% to $0.0247 over the past 24 hours, despite a broader market rally. Bitcoin gained 2.83% to trade above $80,500, supported by a post-election rally and renewed inflows into spot Bitcoin ETFs.

OGN moved in the opposite direction, this suggests some investors may be taking profits or moving funds into larger cryptocurrencies.

OGN’s 24-hour trading volume also increased 8.28% to $4.15 million. However, higher trading activity has not helped the price recover.

If OGN holds above $0.0240, it could trade sideways. A break below this level could push the price toward $0.0230. Bitcoin’s ability to stay above $80,000 may also affect OGN’s next move.

As 2026 enters its final quarter, it will be an important year for Origin Protocol. The coming months will test whether its deflationary token model can help OGN recover. Unlike inflationary DeFi tokens, OGN’s supply is shrinking while staking rewards continue, revenue increases, and TVL grows.

If more people start using OETH across DeFi and more users deposit into OUSD, the protocol’s revenue could increase, which would allow more OGN buybacks.

This could create a positive cycle where more TVL brings more fees, more fees lead to more buybacks, buybacks reduce supply, and lower supply can push the price upward.

However, this whole model depends on people actually using Origin’s yield products, not just market hype or speculation.

#5243. Tesla, Amazon Deal Fresh Blow to OKX Tokenization Push

OKX has suffered another big blow to its grand aspirations of tokenizing stocks after Tesla, Amazon, and four other big names turned down plans for the tokenization of their shares on the cryptocurrency exchange’s joint venture with New York Stock Exchange owner Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).

Six new companies have raised objections to their shares being tokenized on the OKXICE platform.

Among the new objectors are Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX, e-commerce giant Amazon, streaming giant Netflix, semiconductor equipment maker Lam Research and fintech firm SoFi Technologies.

The new objections bring the total number of companies that have objected to the initiative to 56, further damaging OKX’s push into the realm of traditional finance.

In particular, five of the Magnificent Seven tech companies have turned down the proposal to have their stocks tokenized on the OKXICE platform. These include Tesla, Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Nvidia.

What makes this rejection even more noteworthy is that the total number of targeted companies involved in this OKXICE joint venture is relatively low.

Back in early October, OKX and ICE announced their plan to offer tokenized versions of 62 major companies’ stocks.

However, 49 out of those 62 companies have formally opposed the proposal. Hence, about 79% of the initially targeted companies have rejected the plan. The other seven objections came from companies not in the initial selection.

Some of the most famous names in American finance and tech, including JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Walmart, Coca-Cola, Intel, Oracle, AMD, Nike and Costco, have also expressed their objections.

As of the Nov. 2 notice, only 13 out of the original selection had yet to raise a publicly disclosed objection.

These names include Apple, Coinbase, Robinhood, Strategy, Circle and Palantir.

However, the fact that they have not raised a formal objection doesn’t necessarily mean they approve of the tokenization plan.

It is worth noting that Nov. 3 marks the end of the 30-day objection period for the companies that received their initial notice on Oct. 4.

Nonetheless, with almost four-fifths of the initially targeted companies raising objections, OKXICE faces an uphill battle to get sufficient corporate involvement to make its tokenized stock market appealing to investors.

OKXICE has not set a definite launch date yet. It also has not disclosed the number of tokenized stocks it will offer when it starts trading.

#5242. Crypto Hack Losses Hit $8.74 in 2026, More Than Triple 2025, Yet Without Binance the Year Ran Quieter: How Did Bitcoin and Ethereum React After Major Hacks?

Crypto hack losses hit $8.74B in 2026 vs $2.51B in 2025. Here’s how Bitcoin and Ether moved a day, a week and a month after major hacks.

Crypto hack losses reached $8.74 billion in 2026 by October 31, more than three times the $2.51 billion lost over the same ten months of 2025, after the October 29 Binance breach alone added $6.36 billion.

Take Binance out and the picture flips. The rest of 2026 comes to $2.38 billion, about 5% less than 2025 at the same point, even though attackers hit 325 targets against 120 a year earlier. More attacks, smaller hauls, and then one enormous one.

The market has its own pattern. Across the ten largest hacks since January 2025, Bitcoin’s move on the day of the attack ranged from -4.1% to +1.9%. A month later, for the nine with a full month of data, the range ran from -15.5% to +19.9%, and it followed whatever the broader market was doing.

The 2025 hacks landed in falling markets, and every one was followed by a lower Bitcoin price a month later. Most of 2026’s landed in rising ones.

So how bad has 2026 really been, and what does history say about the weeks after Binance?

The size of the biggest theft. Through September, 2026 was running behind 2025: $2.24 billion lost against $2.48 billion. Then Binance lost $6.36 billion across ten blockchains in one night, more than all of 2025’s hacks put together.

The two years share a culprit. The FBI tied 2025’s largest crypto hack, the $1.4 billion Bybit theft on February 21, to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Chainalysis now ties Binance to the same unit. The biggest hacks of each year:

The rest of 2026 looks different from 2025 too. There were 325 incidents through October, almost three times 2025’s 120, and five 2026 hacks topped $290 million, against one in 2025. Stolen keys and cross-chain bridges did most of the damage outside Binance.

The gross number also overstates what stays lost. CertiK’s October tally counts $3.03 billion frozen or returned, mostly Binance funds caught on-chain, which cuts the month’s adjusted losses to about $3.47 billion. Trackers also disagree on the year: CertiK puts 2026 at $9.2 billion gross and 2025 at $3.35 billion, while DefiLlama has $8.74 billion and $2.72 billion.

DISCOVER: Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying

A small dip on the day, then the market’s own trend. The heatmap compares Bitcoin and Ether with their close the day before each of the ten biggest hacks since 2025.

Bybit is the closest match to Binance: a North Korean exchange theft over $1 billion. Bitcoin lost 14.2% within a week of it, with US tariff fears weighing on markets that week too, and it was still 12.4% lower a month on.

Binance is following a gentler path so far. From the October 28 close to Monday:

Neither yet. Bitcoin trades at $77,870 on Binance, flat on the day, and has held above its October 30 low of $76,326 for three days, right on the 200-day EMA (exponential moving average) at $76,512.

After Bybit, Bitcoin lost its floor within a week. After most of 2026’s hacks, it was higher a month later. The line between the two is clear on the chart: the 200-day EMA below, and the 50-day EMA at $80,293 above.

The crypto hack record says the first day rarely decides much. What Bitcoin does at the 200-day EMA over the next few weeks will show which path this one takes.

#5240. Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse Breaks Silence on XRP vs. RLUSD Debate

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse addressed the ongoing debate over the potential impact of Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin on XRP’s future, asserting that both assets are complementary rather than competitive.

On Nov. 3, Brad Garlinghouse offered his view in response to a comprehensive X post from a notable member of the XRP Ledger community named Vet, who outlined the key differences between the two assets associated with Ripple.

“Well said, Vet. Complementary, not competitive,” the Ripple chief executive tweeted.

The brief statement comes amid pushback as some XRP holders are increasingly concerned that Ripple’s aggressive foray into the stablecoin market may negatively impact demand for XRP in the future.

As part of his viral post, Vet explained that the key difference between the two assets revolves around the purposes they serve on the XRP Ledger.

“RLUSD is optional. XRP isn’t,” the commentator explained.

As the XRP Ledger’s native currency, XRP is essential for the core functions of the network. First, every account must have an XRP reserve. Second, transaction fees are paid in XRP.

RLUSD, on the other hand, is a dollar-denominated stablecoin issued by Ripple's regulated stablecoin business. The key difference is that, unlike XRP, the value of RLUSD is supposed to remain stable at roughly $1.

Another key difference lies in control over the assets.

Ripple has the ability to freeze RLUSD under certain conditions, for example, to meet legal obligations. There is no central entity that can freeze XRP, the native cryptocurrency, on the ledger.

According to Vet, another key advantage of XRP is its privileged status on the XRP Ledger's DEX.

The XRP Ledger has an automatic bridging function. In this way, if it makes sense to trade between currencies through XRP for a better exchange rate, trades can be automatically routed through XRP.

This is why XRP is so valuable for liquidity providers and market makers as an intermediary asset.

On the other hand, RLUSD would be much more suitable in cases where price stability is important, for example, for payroll, invoicing, corporate payments, etc.

At the same time, some XRP investors are worried that one day RLUSD may effectively replace XRP for some payment use cases.

The crucial question is this: If you can send a dollar-denominated stablecoin directly, why would you need to use an intermediary like XRP?

It’s also worth noting that RLUSD isn’t exclusive to the XRP Ledger. In fact, RLUSD also works on Ethereum and other supported blockchains. So increasing demand for RLUSD doesn’t necessarily lead to more use of the XRP Ledger.

And even if we’re seeing more RLUSD transactions on the XRP Ledger, this doesn’t automatically mean that increased demand for XRP to pay transaction fees necessarily guarantees a significant price surge for the cryptocurrency.

It’s not the first time Garlinghouse has been forced to comment on Ripple's changing priorities.

During Ripple’s Swell 2026 conference in New York on Oct. 28, Ripple’s CEO directly addressed rumors that Ripple is becoming increasingly focused on RLUSD rather than XRP.

“We will never give up on XRP,” Garlinghouse said.

Bitcoin news: North Korea calls Binance hack claims “absurd” as $3.24B in stolen crypto, mostly BTC and ETH, sits in hacker wallets.

In Bitcoin news on Tuesday, November 3, North Korea rejected US claims that its hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, as Kim Yo Jong called the FBI’s attribution “absurd rhetoric” and suggested that Washington itself might be behind the heist.

The statement, carried by the state news agency KCNA, came three days after the FBI named TraderTraitor, a North Korean state hacking unit, as the culprit.

#5237. Top Wallet-as-a-Service Providers for Ethereum in 2026

Disclaimer: The below article is sponsored, and the views in it do not represent those of ZyCrypto. Readers should conduct independent research before taking any actions related to the project mentioned in this piece. This article should not be regarded as investment advice.

How Aligned, Privy, Dynamic, Turnkey, and Magic compare

A small group of established providers leads wallet-as-a-service solutions (WaaS) on Ethereum, including Aligned, Privy, Dynamic, Turnkey, and Magic. All are non-custodial and primarily compete on four things: how they secure the key, how they handle accounts and gas, how much of the stack they cover, and who owns the company.

For a consumer app or a financial institution building on Ethereum, the wallet is the integration you most want to get right the first time. It’s what users touch directly and trust with their funds, and it signs every transaction they make. It’s also the decision that compounds: once people hold balances, switching providers means migrating live accounts, so getting it right early pays off most.

Today’s leading WaaS providers look almost identical on the surface. They’re all non-custodial, and they all spare users the crypto mechanics: no seed phrase, no gas token, no contract prompts to approve. The differences that shape an integration sit underneath: the key-security model, how accounts and gas work, how much of the stack comes from one vendor, and who owns that vendor.

The field of credible wallet providers is small but far from uniform. Each was built around a different priority, and they overlap enough to blur together. Understanding what each one is keeps the biggest name from standing in for the best fit.

Aligned: Independent, founded by the team behind LambdaClass, and the only provider in the group focused exclusively on Ethereum: it runs on Ethereum L1 and on ZK rollups built with ethrex, while the others prioritize multichain reach. Every account is an EIP-7702 smart account that requires two signatures: one from the user’s key on their device and one from Aligned’s backend. It ships as part of a larger stack, with the rollup, proof aggregation, and interoperability all coming from the same team. Sovra runs identity for 8M+ people on it.

Privy (Stripe): The most widely deployed of the group by self-reported counts, with 200M+ accounts and customers like Hyperliquid and Ramp. It splits each key into two Shamir shares, both held on Privy’s side (one inside a secure enclave), and reassembles the key only inside the enclave. Its default EOA wallet can be upgraded in place through EIP-7702, or act as the signer of a separate ERC-4337 smart wallet. It carries several independent audits plus SOC 2 Type I and Type II.

Dynamic (Fireblocks): As much a login-and-wallet-connection platform as an embedded wallet, with a wide range of sign-in methods and connectors to 800+ external wallets. That fits apps where plenty of users already have a wallet, alongside those who need one made. Its keys use threshold-signature MPC. Customers have included Kraken and Ondo.

Turnkey: The signing and key-management foundation other wallets build on. It generates and uses raw private keys inside secure enclaves, with a policy engine that checks every signature. Of the enclave-based providers, Turnkey is the one that lets you verify the enclave itself: reproducible builds and remote attestation confirm the exact code that touched the key. Independent, founded by an ex-Coinbase Custody team. Customers include Bridge and Polymarket.

Magic: The oldest of the group, launched in 2018 and known for email-first onboarding. It protects keys with a mix of secure enclaves, a cloud key-management service, and sharding, and it holds the widest set of compliance certifications in the group: SOC 2, SOC 3, and ISO 27001. Its wallet business is being acquired by Payward, Kraken’s parent company, in a deal agreed in July 2026.

Most top WaaS solutions today are non-custodial, meaning they can’t move users’ funds without their consent. But that label covers a wide range: how much you trust the provider depends on how it handles the private key, and that trust underpins what you can promise users about their money. The clearest divide is whether the full key is ever assembled in one place, and it splits these solutions into two camps.

All three bring the full key together inside secure hardware, and they differ only on when. Privy splits it into two Shamir shares (not MPC), both held on its side, and reassembles them in a TEE at signing. Magic does the same with a TEE, a cloud key-management service, and sharding. Turnkey skips reassembly, keeping raw keys inside secure enclaves full-time behind a policy engine. Either way, the enclave exposes the full key, so its integrity is the security boundary.

Each gives you a different way to trust that boundary. Turnkey makes the enclave verifiable through open-source enclave code, reproducible builds, and remote attestation, so you can confirm the exact code handling the key. Privy leans on outside audits from Cure53, Zellic, and Doyensec, and Magic on the widest set of certifications in the group, SOC 2, SOC 3, and ISO 27001.

Dynamic and Aligned take the enclave out of the picture: no single key can move funds on its own, and they get there two ways. Dynamic uses threshold-signature MPC, where independent parties each hold a share and sign jointly, so no machine, Dynamic’s included, ever holds a spendable key. Aligned uses two separate keys and requires both to sign. The user’s key stays on their device (a WebAuthn passkey, a P-256 key, or an ECDSA key), Aligned’s key stays on its backend, and the account contract checks both signatures on-chain before it executes anything. Passkeys are verified on-chain as P-256 signatures inside the WebAuthn envelope. A breach of Aligned’s backend doesn’t move funds, and neither does a stolen device on its own.

The trade-off to plan for is availability: a signature needs a second party online. The two handle that differently. Dynamic’s 2-of-3 option lets any two of the three shares sign, so one being offline won’t lock the wallet. Aligned’s 2-of-2 doesn’t have that cushion: every transaction needs Aligned’s co-signer, so access depends on its backend staying reachable. For lost devices, Aligned offers optional guardian recovery: the guardian is set per app, and the timelock per account. The guardian can add a new key to an account, but that key can’t sign until a timelock expires (1 to 14 days, fixed when the account is created), which leaves a window to cancel an unwanted recovery. Accounts created without a timelock have no guardian.

One more point of trust sits above the accounts themselves. Aligned accounts route through a beacon contract, one per app, and the beacon’s owner can rotate the signers and point accounts to a new implementation without touching each one. That makes upgrades and key rotation simple to operate, and it means teams should know who controls the beacon for their app.

On its own, an Ethereum account is bare: a user needs ETH to do anything, every action is a separate approval, and losing the key means losing the funds. Account abstraction lifts those limits by giving the account programmable logic, so a product can cover gas for users, batch several steps into one confirmation, and offer recovery. All of them do this. They differ in the underlying standard, and providers are split between them.

ERC-4337 is the longest-running route, and Privy’s smart wallets build on ERC-4337. It works entirely at the application layer: user actions become “UserOperation” objects that a separate mempool and “bundler” services collect, batch, and submit through a shared EntryPoint contract, with an optional paymaster covering gas. Because it needs no change to Ethereum itself, it went live on Ethereum mainnet in March 2023 and now has the deepest audit and tooling history of any account-abstraction approach.

That maturity comes with operational overhead. Each user needs a separate smart-contract account deployed and maintained, and much of the market reaches 4337 through shared third-party middleware such as ZeroDev. It’s a well-worn path, and it also puts a common external layer in the critical signing path for many apps at once, which is worth weighing at institutional scale.

Aligned builds on EIP-7702, a 2025 protocol change that landed in Ethereum’s Pectra upgrade. It lets an ordinary account (an EOA) point to contract code and run it directly, so a user’s existing address gains smart-account behavior without deploying a second account alongside it. Aligned uses 7702 on its own, with no 4337 EntryPoint, bundler, or paymaster: its backend submits each transaction and pays the gas, so users never need to hold ETH or the chain’s native token. The result is leaner: one address, nothing extra to deploy or fund, and no third-party middleware between the user and the chain. Because it depends on 7702, it runs only on chains that have adopted Pectra.

EIP-7702 and ERC-4337 aren’t mutually exclusive: Privy signs 7702 authorizations for any implementation, Dynamic and Magic now offer 7702-based smart accounts, and Turnkey, as a pure signer, handles both transaction types and leaves the account model to you. Which one fits depends on whether a team wants established 4337 tooling or a simpler account with fewer moving parts.

Providers also differ in how much of the wallet you build yourself. The options fall on three levels, from a bare signing primitive you wrap in your own code to a full stack that arrives assembled. Where a provider sits decides how many vendors you take on and how independent the pieces of your stack stay.

Turnkey sits lowest, by design. It hands you a signing and key-management foundation and leaves the account-abstraction layer, gas handling, and smart-account logic for you to build. That’s the most work and the most control. Your wallet logic stays independent of any one chain or vendor, and signing sits behind a boundary you can attest. Teams with their own engineers often start here for that reason.

Privy, Dynamic, and Magic sit in the middle, as full embedded-wallet SDKs. They handle onboarding, key security, and gas, while you bring the chain and settle wherever you like. Dynamic leans hardest into authentication and wallet connection, with 800+ external-wallet connectors, so it suits apps where many users show up with a wallet already.

Aligned sits at the other end and sells the most in one piece: the wallet plus a rollup and proof aggregation, with interoperability, all from one team. Its ZK rollups are built with ethrex, the Rust Ethereum client from LambdaClass, and settle on Ethereum. That folds several procurement and integration decisions into one, and removes the seams between those layers.

It also concentrates your dependencies. The wallet, chain, and settlement all come from one provider, so they move together on a single roadmap and a single uptime, and more of your stack rides on one vendor. An institution gets one supplier to vet, and one point of dependence to weigh in return.

A wallet provider is a long-term dependency, so the decision comes down to a few things each team has to settle: how much to trust a provider with key handling, how much of the account and gas experience to hand off, and how much of the stack to source from one vendor.

The demo won’t decide it for you, because they all deliver the same clean experience: no seed phrase, no gas token, a smooth login. Their real differences sit underneath, in the two choices hardest to reverse once users hold funds: how the key is secured, and how much of the product leans on a single company. Past that, the best fit depends on what you’re building and what stage it’s at.

Provider details, figures, and ownership information were checked against public sources as of November 2026 and may change; teams should confirm them with each provider before choosing one.

#5232. Binance Hacker Continues Aggressive Bitcoin Buying Spree

The hacker behind the monumental Binance attack is still buying up more Bitcoin (BTC).

As per the latest blockchain analytics data from Lookonchain dated Nov. 4, the hacker continues to exchange SOL for Bitcoin, moving the stolen assets across several crypto wallets.

The blockchain tracker added that the hacker is using the following multi-step process to exchange the stolen crypto for Bitcoin.

The hacker’s complicated scheme involves splitting his SOL assets among different wallets before selling the SOL for USDC, transferring the USDC from Solana to Ethereum, buying ETH using the USDC and finally exchanging the newly bought ETH for BTC using THORChain, a decentralized cross-chain liquidity protocol.

This long and complicated cross-chain transaction process allows the hacker to easily transfer his funds between different blockchain networks. It also makes it harder to trace the stolen assets.

This in not the first time that the hacker has been buying Bitcoin with the stolen funds. In fact, he had earlier been seen making transactions to buy Bitcoin using tens of millions of dollars’ worth of stolen SOL.

As per Lookonchain’s data dated Nov. 1, the hacker behind the Binance hack was trying to convert approximately 970,522 SOL, worth roughly $95.9 million at the time of writing, into Bitcoin.

The hacker was even seen making a transaction involving 486,970 SOL (approximately $46.4M) in just one hour.

However, during these transactions, the hacker used a different service called Relay Protocol, which also allows cross-chain crypto transfers.

From the recent blockchain data, it looks like the hacker is still focused on Bitcoin. He’s also using several decentralized services to exchange the stolen crypto.

The latest official update from Binance shows that the massive security breach has affected crypto assets worth around $6.34 billion.

As per the update, the exchange says that it has frozen/intercepted about $2.85 billion worth of stolen cryptocurrency as of Nov. 3.

According to US federal authorities, the attack was conducted by a North Korean state-sponsored hacker group called TraderTraitor.

The FBI is also asking various decentralized crypto services like THORChain to prevent funds linked to the attack from moving around.

Even with all these efforts, the latest on-chain data shows that the hacker is still moving stolen funds across different networks.

#5220. Solana Co-Founder Names Biggest Threat to Crypto

Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko said phishing and social engineering attacks are the biggest threat to crypto and advised investors to worry more about social engineering attacks than about AI or quantum computers breaking crypto security.

"Phishing and social engineering is the biggest threat to crypto. Not AI breaking math or quantum computers," he wrote on X.

The Solana co-founder also suggested having a separate iOS device with Apple's Lockdown Mode turned on and using a multisignature crypto wallet.

This is one of the cheapest ways for investors to safeguard their digital assets, according to Yakovenko.

The Solana co-founder's statement highlights a fundamental weakness in crypto security: hackers don't need to break blockchain security to steal digital assets.

What they can do is fool crypto holders into giving them access to their assets.

Phishing involves using malicious emails, sites or messages to trick people into revealing sensitive information such as crypto wallet recovery phrases, account information, etc.

Social engineering is a broader term that describes attacks in which hackers manipulate victims into doing something that can compromise their security.

Yakovenko's point becomes crystal clear with the recent massive hack at Binance.

The world's largest crypto exchange, Binance, faced a security breach on Oct. 29 that affected around $6.34 billion in digital assets.

According to Binance's Nov. 3 investigation update, the hackers carried out a sophisticated social engineering attack, which included fake job interviews to compromise Binance employees.

A Binance software engineer was targeted by people pretending to be representatives of a fake company. The Binance employee went through some fake job interviews. The employee was convinced to download what seemed to be a legitimate technical assignment.

But the downloaded file contained malicious code that helped the hackers compromise the employee's computer.

Then, the hackers used the compromised devices, stolen credentials and an internal AI tool to access Binance's wallet infrastructure.

Eventually, this helped the hackers execute unauthorized crypto transfers from the exchange's hot wallets.

The Security Alliance (SEAL) released a report on Nov. 4 stating that its security team handled 99 incidents from Oct. 28 to Nov. 3.

In three of those incidents involving fraudulent customer support calls, victims lost roughly $1.57 million and 1.12 BTC from Oct. 28 to Nov. 3.

One of the scams involved fake Apple support representatives stealing a victim's Apple ID credentials. The victim had saved their crypto recovery phrase in cloud storage. Another victim shared their wallet recovery phrase during a fake Telegram support call.

The group also tracked 5,137 phishing domains during this reporting period.

#5219. Cboe and Citadel Sue to Stop US Stock Perps Hours After the CFTC Approved Them: Why Hyperliquid’s $5 Billion-a-Day Market Has the Most at Stake

Cboe and Citadel want US stock perps blocked. Hyperliquid already trades $5B of them a day, and ICE wants to bring it onshore.

A group backed by Cboe and Citadel Securities sued the CFTC on Tuesday, November 3, to block stock perps hours after the regulator cleared them for US exchanges, a fight that could decide whether Hyperliquid’s $5 billion-a-day market reaches American traders. The approval named no offshore venue, but it was aimed at one.

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said Americans should not be “forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues” to trade perpetual futures on individual stocks.

🇺🇸 A CBOE AND CITADEL SECURITIES-BACKED GROUP SUES THE CFTC TO BLOCK PERPETUAL FUTURES ON US STOCKS, THE SAME DAY THE CFTC APPROVED THEM pic.twitter.com/38PNXGcM5f

— The Wolf Of All Streets (@scottmelker) November 3, 2026

The biggest of those venues runs on Hyperliquid. Trade.xyz, its largest builder market, did $4.99 billion in volume over the past 24 hours across 142 contracts on stocks, indexes and commodities, with $4.42 billion in open interest.

Six days ago, NYSE owner ICE agreed to bring those markets to US traders through a CFTC-regulated exchange of its own. HYPE jumped as much as 21% that day, to $97.74, just short of its $97.96 record.

The lawsuit didn’t knock it over. HYPE dipped to $81.01 early Wednesday and was back at $85.93 by 08:00 UTC, up 2.8% in 24 hours.

So what is the lawsuit about, and what does it mean for perp DEXs like Hyperliquid?

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

Who gets to regulate single-stock perpetuals?  The Capital Markets Alliance, whose members include Cboe, Citadel Securities and the Healthy Markets Association, filed in federal court in Manhattan. It argues the contracts are security-based swaps, which belong to the SEC and are kept away from retail investors.

“This issue, however, is about investor protection for securities trading and the rule of law,” Cboe CEO Craig Donohue said.

The CFTC hit back. “Our markets should be governed by law, not litigation campaigns intended to block innovation,” a spokesperson said.

Four exchanges are waiting on the outcome. Kalshi filed first, on September 18, followed by Coinbase Derivatives, Bitnomial and Crypto.com’s North American Derivatives Exchange. CME Group is already suing the CFTC over Kalshi’s Bitcoin perpetual, approved in May.

DISCOVER: Ripple Prime Opens 24/7 RWA Perpetual Swaps: Institutional Capital Hits Tokenized Stocks and Commodities

Big enough to rival its crypto markets. Hyperliquid’s own crypto perpetuals did $7.14 billion over the same 24 hours, so trade.xyz’s markets made up about 41% of everything traded on the chain.

Indexes and oil lead, but single stocks fill most of the list:

Trade.xyz launched in October 2025 as the first market built on HIP-3, Hyperliquid’s system that lets outside teams list their own contracts. It now handles about 98% of HIP-3 volume and says it has processed $650 billion in total trading.

It is built for traders outside the US. Hyperliquid blocks US users on its own front end, and that is the gap Selig wants US exchanges to fill.

Very little for its markets today, and a lot for its path into the US. The case can’t touch trades on Hyperliquid itself. What it decides is whether American exchanges can compete for the same flow, and whether ICE can bring trade.xyz onshore.

The two outcomes cut in opposite directions:

Neither will happen soon. ICE’s exchange still needs its own CFTC approval, and neither company has given a launch date.

The first real test comes sooner. The court still has to decide whether to freeze the approval while the case runs. A freeze would stall US listings before Kalshi or Coinbase trade a single contract.

EXPLORE: HYPE Jumps +23% as CFTC Pathway Raises Hyperliquid US Market Hopes

HYPE has given back most of last week’s ICE spike. It hit $97.74 on October 29, slid back over the next few days, and now trades at $85.93, just above its 20-day EMA of $84.02.

For now, the fight over stock perps is about who can sell them to Americans. Hyperliquid already sells them to everyone else, $5 billion a day of it.

#5217. Can You Put Crypto Mining in Space? Elon Musk's Data Center Idea Can Be Used in Crypto

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Elon Musk did what he does best on X: fresh speculations via post on November 4, saying: “Data centers in space look pretty appealing right now.”

Musk was talking about data centers, but the idea can be used in crypto too: could Bitcoin mining rigs work in orbit, powered only by the Sun? Technically, they should, why not? Economically, however, it's getting a bit more complicated.

Space has one big advantage: plenty of solar energy. Unlike mining farms on Earth, orbital mining stations could use large solar ray to make their own electricity without any power grid. Satellites today could get constant powering from sunlight, leading to a lower battery consumption.

Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now

In theory, Bitcoin ASIC miners could then run around the clock with very low or non-existent ongoing electricity costs. The problem is that solar panels, batteries, power electronics and would all have to be launched into orbit–that's the part where problems arise.

Space might look like the perfect place to cool mining equipment, since the cosmic background is extremely cold. Unfortunately, it's not so simple and the vacuum in space actually makes cooling harder than on earth.

Here, mining rigs get rid of heat with fans, air conditioning or liquid cooling, in orbit, there's no air at all that will be able to push the air away. So the only option out there seems to be the liquid cooling, large radiator panels which should be able to release heat as infrared radiation.

According to Boston Consulting Group (BCG), a 100-kilowatt orbital data center could need around a whopping 400 square meters of radiators. But apart from technical challenges, we should always keep in mind the profitability. Getting equipment to space in the first place is what makes the whole idea questionable.

According to BCG, launching to orbit currently costs around $1,500 per kilogram. That means, a one-ton mining setup would cost around $1.5 million just to launch, excluding hardware, cooling, solar arrays and maintenance that will cost just as much if not more.

You also can't ignore space radiation, equipment failures and limited chances for repairs that add even more costs at the top of it. The only thing that can somehow make math look better is more efficient ASIC chips and ways of delivering goods to space at the fraction of today's costs.

Thankfully, Bitcoin miners need little to no bandwidth, so the connection issue is somewhat solved on its own.

Physically, mining Bitcoin in space is possible: is it justifiable financially though? Not really. Reusable rockets, lightweight cooling and other things might make it more financially viable, but as of today, we should be sticking with good old mining rigs in huge hangars on Earth.

Dogecoin community member Mishaboar has shared a fresh safety reminder to DOGE holders as cryptocurrency withdrawals resume on Binance following the exchange's recent security incident.

Binance began restoring withdrawals in phases on November 1, 2026, with that of Dogecoin already restored. Binance has also published a cryptographic Proof of Reserves for selected assets, including Dogecoin, based on its October 31 snapshot.

A few updates on the Binance situation since my last post. - The Hack Binance has finally published its initial technical findings, and, as we had expected, the attack was considerably more complicated than the original explanation involving a compromised devops laptop. According to Binance, the attackers targeted multiple engineers through malicious software, including an earlier attempt involving a tampered devtool installer and a fake job interview that delivered malware. They then exploited an internal AI tool and stolen deployment credentials to gain access to Binance's wallet-signing infrastructure. On Ethereum, malicious EIP-7702 authorizations allowed the attackers to continue moving funds even after Binance had suspended normal withdrawals. It's difficult to understand why the signing controls allowed these authorizations in the first place. I am curious to know how it is possible the authorizations were not detected more quickly, and why revoking them took so long on wallets holding such gigantic amounts. Binance says it took almost four hours to fully contain the attack. It will be good to see independent reviews from competent security analysts. - Withdrawals/Deposits (after withdrawals reopened) According to figures shared by Binance co-CEO Richard Teng and reported by CoinDesk, approximately $10.97 billion was withdrawn during the first 46 hours after withdrawals reopened, against $5.69 billion in deposits. That leaves approximately $5.28 billion in net outflows, as of early November 3. Withdrawal activity was particularly intense on Sunday, but appears to have slowed down since. Binance claims that hourly deposits had started exceeding withdrawals by the end of that period. - The Money Binance reported approximately $2.85 billion frozen or intercepted in its November 3 update. Once again, remember that frozen funds are NOT necessarily recovered funds. Binance also says it has replaced the vast majority of affected assets using its own resources, including SAFU and insurance funds (see my previous update for considerations about this). The published replenishment percentages have been somewhat inconsistent, however. And once again, replacing stolen assets is NOT the same as recovering them from the attackers. Using SAFU and the Futures Insurance Fund to cover these losses also means that the risk profile of holding funds on the exchange may have shifted considerably. As exchanges operate largely within black boxes, it is difficult to assess this at this point. - Withdrawals and Proof of Reserves Binance has published a cryptographic Proof of Reserves for ten selected assets (including Dogecoin), based on its October 31 snapshot. That is considerably fewer than the 55 assets covered in its previous snapshot, with many smaller assets still missing. Once again, this is useful, but as I have explained multiple times, Proof of Reserves are never a comprehensive audit of an exchange's financial condition and stability. More cryptocurrency withdrawals are being restored in phases, although availability still depends on the specific asset and network. Native Dogecoin withdrawals were included in the first reopening phase. The usual reminder: please make sure you select the actual Dogecoin network when withdrawing to your own wallet, rather than stuff like Binance-pegged DOGE on BSC. My recommendation stays the same: withdraw when and if you can, without rushing, and after verifying that you have good backups of your wallets and that the wallet you are using is safe.

As native Dogecoin withdrawals have now been restored, Mishaboar shared his "usual reminder" to the Dogecoin community, telling them to ensure they select the actual Dogecoin network when withdrawing to their wallets, "rather than stuff like Binance-pegged DOGE on BSC," he said.

A Binance-Pegged Dogecoin, a BEP-20 token, runs on the BNB Smart Chain (BSC), and the distinction between it and the actual DOGE coin on the Dogecoin network remains essential to prevent confusion.

Mishaboar also advised users not to rush the withdrawal process, noting that wallet security and proper backup procedures should come first: "My recommendation remains the same: withdraw when and if you can, without rushing, and after verifying that you have good backups of your wallets and that the wallet you are using is secure."

Major crypto exchange Binance recently published initial findings and a response update on the October 29 security incident.

According to Binance, the attackers targeted multiple engineers through malicious software, including an earlier attempt involving a tampered devtool installer and a fake job interview that delivered malware. They then exploited an internal AI tool and stolen deployment credentials to gain access to Binance's wallet-signing infrastructure.

The incident involves assets of some $6.34 billion. About $2.85 billion worth of assets have been intercepted or frozen as of the update.

As of Oct. 31, 2026, Binance said it has restored 98% of the affected token assets and is working on purchasing outstanding, more illiquid assets.

Binance stated that the entry points identified as having been used in the attack have been closed, and it is engaging independent third-party cybersecurity experts to conduct a comprehensive review of the incident.
