Bitcoin (BTC) is back on its feet above the psychologically important $80,000 level after dipping to about $75,600 with the help of a fresh buying interest. Shiba Inu (SHIB) isn't joining the party, though, and stays under substantial selling pressure.

BTC was trading around $80,300 on November 5, up more than 3% over 24 hours. Ether did even better, gaining about 5% to roughly $2,421, so the weakness looks specific to SHIB rather than to the whole altcoin market.

The jump looks like a short squeeze: about $378 million in short positions were liquidated within a single hour, and total liquidations reached around $747 million, according to CoinGlass. Spot Bitcoin ETFs also stopped bleeding. Outflows of about $1.16 billion across October 30, November 2 and November 3 gave way to a $74.6 million net inflow on November 4, according to Farside, although BlackRock's IBIT still lost $201.2 million that day.

Unfortunately, short covering alone doesn't prove fresh demand, and CryptoQuant analyst CryptoZeno argues the correction may not be over, pointing to the Bitcoin Cycle Extremes Index sitting at 15.8% on its 30-day average.

On the daily chart, buyers absorbed the selling near the 200-day moving average in the $76,000–$77,000 support region, and BTC then climbed back above its shorter-term moving averages. The relative strength index (RSI) is around 51, up from weaker readings, so momentum is improving, but a bullish reversal isn't confirmed yet.

XRP, Solana and BNB added roughly 2–4% over the same 24 hours, but Shiba Inu hasn't managed a proper recovery. SHIB is trading near $0.00000475, well below its September highs around $0.00000620.

The token has also broken below its ascending support trendline, invalidating the previously positive technical structure, and it stays below its major moving averages, which increasingly act as resistance rather than support. The closest resistance zone is around $0.00000510–$0.00000530, while stronger resistance remains near $0.00000550.

Although the RSI is approaching oversold territory, there's not enough evidence of proper accumulation yet.

#5166. What Is RED-S? Doctors Explain the Condition—and Why Women Are at Higher Risk

When it comes to exercise, there’s one thing that’s just as important as the training itself: fueling. Having the right nutrients—and enough calories—to sustain your activity and recover from it are critical for staying healthy, feeling your best, and keeping your body functioning in tip-top shape. After all, fueling your body isn't just about performing well today; it's about being able to keep doing what you love for years to come.

Eating can sometimes feel like an afterthought, especially when you’re busy with training, but consistently underfueling can actually result in a condition called relative energy deficiency in sport, or RED-S for short. And women have a much higher risk of developing RED-S compared to men. In a 2026 study in the Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport, researchers found that 70 percent of high-level female athletes were at risk of developing RED-S.

Top-ranked tennis player Emma Navarro recently revealed that she is one of those athletes dealing with the condition. Earlier this month, she posted on Instagram, detailing her experience, which included extreme mood swings, brain fog, a weakened immune system, constant headaches, and bouts of dizziness. Exercises she could do with ease in the past suddenly felt impossible. She was also hungry, all the time. “I had been under-fueling for almost three years,” she wrote. “My body was fighting back any way it knew how.”

But, you don’t need to be an elite-level tennis player to experience the condition. Here’s what you need to know about RED-S, including how to spot—and stop—it early, according to experts.

Meet the experts: Elizabeth Matzkin, MD, is an orthopedic surgeon and chief of women’s sports medicine at Brigham and Women’s Hospital. Amy West, MD, is a sports medicine physician at Northwell Orthopedic Institute. Amy Stephens, RD, is a sports dietitian who specializes in eating disorders.

There’s a simple explanation behind what causes RED-S: It occurs when someone is not eating enough to meet the demands of their training—or even their body’s basic physiologic needs, says Elizabeth Matzkin, MD, an orthopedic surgeon and chief of women’s sports medicine at Brigham and Women’s Hospital. Your body needs energy not only to sustain you, say, on a run or in a weightlifting session, but it also needs energy to support bone health, hormone production, metabolism, immune function, and cardiovascular health.

When you’re consistently not consuming enough food to support your activity levels, over time, your body won’t have the energy it needs to support those critical functions, leading to a wide range of symptoms that define RED-S—which is more than medical jargon for undereating. It reflects what happens when your body is chronically underfueled and can lead to long-term health issues.

Anyone, from the elite athlete to someone training for their first half-marathon to the person increasing their lifting sessions in the gym while trying to lose weight, can be at risk of developing RED-S. Remember, the “r” in RED-S stands for relative; so it’s all about not meeting your energy needs, whatever they are.

When underfueling, in the short term, you may experience fatigue, impaired concentration, more frequent illnesses, poor recovery, and irregular periods or none at all, Dr. Matzkin says. When it comes to your sport, training and performance may suffer too. Low energy availability can make it harder to sustain a workout, decrease strength and endurance, or lead to muscle weakness or pain, says Amy West, MD, a sports medicine physician at Northwell Orthopedic Institute.

You’ll also be much more susceptible to injuries, particularly when it comes to your bones. This has impacts on the long term: “Adolescence and young adulthood are critical years for building peak bone mass, so prolonged low energy availability during this period may have consequences later in life,” Dr. Matzkin says. Down the line, that could mean osteoporosis. Meanwhile, missing your period for long periods of time can have impacts on future fertility, Dr. West adds.

Early stages of RED-S can happen pretty quickly, says Amy Stephens, RD, a sports dietitian who specializes in eating disorders. After just one day of underfueling, you’ll feel symptoms of “hanger”; after just a week, your body may stop building muscle and endurance. Then, she says, it could take six to nine months to fully recover.

RED-S is much more associated with women and girls compared to boys and men. Until 2014, RED-S was referred to as the “female athlete triad,” which highlighted the relationship between undereating, menstrual dysfunction, and decreased bone mineral density. While RED-S can happen to anyone, “female athletes are more vulnerable, especially in sports that emphasize leanness, endurance, aesthetics, or weight categories,” Dr. Matzkin says. (Think: Running, gymnastics, and diving.)

But, that’s not the only reason women may deal with RED-S more than men. There’s also the pressures that women face disproportionately to be thin, says Dr. West, and the fact that women are more likely to have eating disorders.

RED-S doesn’t happen all at once. Earlier, more subtle signs like fatigue and trouble sleeping pop up when a person has what docs call low energy availability, which occurs when they’re not eating enough to support their activity levels. As someone is continuously in a state of low energy availability, RED-S can occur.

Low energy availability and RED-S can affect almost every system in the body, but these are the areas you may most often see symptoms, according to the doctors.

If RED-S is suddenly on your radar now, don’t worry. You don’t need to completely overhaul your life or your training to avoid it. In fact, there are a few intuitive steps you can take to give yourself a good shot at fueling fully—no calorie tracking necessary. Here’s what you can do.

It’s so simple, but occasionally taking stock of how you’re feeling in and out of training can go a long way. The symptoms above are warning signs of not eating enough, but you should also know what a fully-fueled athlete feels like too. A well-fueled athlete has consistent energy all day, mostly only feels hungry around mealtimes, and doesn’t deal with brain fog, Stephens says. Their mood is stable, they recover well between workouts, and they sleep well too. It’s a good idea to check in and reflect on how you’ve been feeling lately—strong and energized and able to “kick” at the end of a workout, or sluggish and hungry, struggling to get in those last few reps.

Plus, if you wanted to dig even deeper, you can also get some more information from an annual blood workup with your doctor. Since RED-S affects so many systems in the body, Stephens says, you might see issues pop up across a range of tests, including your thyroid, white blood cell count, ferritin and iron, vitamin D, or complete blood count. If any of those are out of range, it could be due to underfueling, but they would need to be discussed with your doctor in the context of the rest of your health history and any other testing.

You don’t need to download a macro-tracking app or suddenly start counting calories to avoid RED-S. (For the record: Stephens doesn’t have her athletes do that.) Instead, focus simply on getting three meals per day, with your plate being about one-third protein, one-third carbs, and one-third vegetables each time. Most people don’t eat breakfast, Stephens says, and that’s often one of the quickest culprits when it comes to not having enough food in a day.

This is another simple reminder, but if you’re someone with a training plan on the horizon, keep in mind that what you’re eating now is not what you’ll be eating in the future, Stephens says. As plans progress and get more and more intense (you’re running longer distances or lifting heavier in the gym or simply adding another day of Solidcore per week), you’ll need to increase the amount of food you eat.

One helpful rule of thumb is that for every hour you spend working out, you should add on an extra 500 to 600 calories to your day, whether that’s with the help of snacks or larger serving sizes at meals, Stephens says. Then, anything in the 2-to-3-hour range will require in-session fueling, like gels on a long run.

If you’re noticing any of the above symptoms or suspect that you’re not fueling right, it’s a good idea to see a professional. Earlier signs like fatigue and poor sleep are easy to write off, but checking in and making sure they’re not a result of underfueling can keep low energy availability from developing into a full-on case of RED-S. In addition to setting an appointment with a doc, you can also try increasing your food intake by incorporating more snacks throughout your day or having larger portion sizes at meals. If you’re not already having a carb-rich snack before a workout, try adding that for some extra energy, paired with something high in protein and carbs afterward to support recovery.

Just keep in mind: It’s never too early to bring this up with a doctor or dietitian, whether you want help determining the appropriate calorie and macro goals for your workout demands or for them to evaluate symptoms you’re not so sure about. “Earlier evaluation is better,” Dr. Matzkin says. “We don't want to wait for a stress fracture—this means bone health has already been affected.” Ideally, you’ll talk with a doctor before reaching this point, but two symptoms that should send you to their office ASAP are frequent injuries, especially if you’re having a tough time recovering from them, and period irregularities, Dr. West says.

From there, treating RED-S is all about getting your body back to the right balance of energy intake to energy output and managing any injuries that may have arisen. You’ll likely need to work with a doctor and/or dietitian to help you get enough calories and nutrients and reduce your training demands while you get caught up. In addition to a sports medicine doc and/or dietitian, you may also work with a bone endocrine specialist (if your bone health has been affected) and/or a sports psychologist, Dr. Matzkin says.

Whether you are at risk for RED-S or not, consider this your reminder that fueling is critical for any active person. Being thoughtful about getting enough calories, carbs, and fat for energy, and protein for recovery is your best line of defense against the condition. While everyone’s needs will be different, a rule of thumb, per Dr. West: “Athletes often need more food than they think.”

Olivia Luppino is an associate editor at Women’s Health. She reports, writes, and edits content ranging from service stories to in-depth features and awards packages across all verticals, including health, fitness, sports, and beauty. While at WH, she’s traveled to Paris, France to watch Faith Kipyegon attempt a sub-4-minute mile and covered major races like Ultra Trail du Mont Blanc in Chamonix. Olivia is a RRCA-certified running coach who is especially passionate about helping people start their running journey and is training for her second marathon. #5165. Cardano Eyes 2,000% Replay From Current Base

Home » Crypto Market News » Cardano Eyes 2,000% Replay From Current Base

As 131 million ADA tokens sit idle in retired pools, the weekly chart structure points to $1.37 as next-cycle destination.

Cardano is trading near $0.19 on a weekly chart that one analyst compares directly to the base that preceded a roughly 2,000% rally in the last cycle. At the same time, on-chain data shows 131.63 million ADA remains tied to retired stake pools, leaving tens of thousands of holders without rewards until they redelegate.

360Trader highlighted the weekly structure and noted that ADA remains well below the level where a true bull-market stage would begin. That stage, in the analyst’s view, only starts once price clears $1.37.

The more immediate requirement is a reclaim of $0.25. Until then the chart is still forming the same kind of low base that previously launched a 2,000% advance once the broader altcoin market turned. The comparison is structural rather than a near-term price target.

Chart Request winner: $ADA 📊Weekly chart, and it's still well under its bull-market stage. That stage really doesn't start until $1.37 breaks.First it needs to get back above $0.25 quickly before I'd be interested.Last cycle ADA went 2000% off a base just like this one.… pic.twitter.com/4BPAusTmTY

From current levels a move to the prior cycle high would still require a multi-hundred-percent gain, and the larger $1.37 threshold sits even further away.

ADA has not yet reclaimed $0.25, the level 360Trader said would be needed before the setup becomes interesting again. The token has been consolidating near the lower end of its multi-year range while the wider crypto market digests recent pressure.

The analyst’s point is that the base itself is not the signal. Confirmation only arrives when price begins to push out of the accumulation zone and the broader altcoin cycle starts to expand.

Until those conditions appear, the historical 2,000% precedent remains a reminder of what has happened from comparable structures rather than a forecast for the next few weeks.

In related Cardano news, Cexplorer data flagged a practical on-chain issue. Roughly 59,025 delegators still have funds assigned to 2,720 retired stake pools, totaling 131.63 million ADA.

Those pools no longer produce blocks or distribute rewards. Holders retain full control of their tokens and can move the delegation to an active pool at any time. The funds are not locked or lost, but every epoch spent on a retired pool is simply a missed reward.

Cardano Has a 131M ADA Staking ProblemThousands of Cardano (@Cardano) holders may need to check where their $ADA is delegated.Cexplorer reports that 59,025 delegators still have funds assigned to retired stake pools. The total comes to 131.63 million ADA.The explorer… pic.twitter.com/cdTn46aFLr

Community responses noted that checking a pool’s status on an explorer and redelegating takes only a minute and restores eligibility for the next epoch’s rewards.

The technical observation and the staking data sit side by side. One points to a historical base that once produced a 2,000% move once conditions aligned.

The other shows that a measurable portion of the staked supply is currently idle because pool operators retired and holders have not yet updated their delegations.

ADA remains near $0.19, below the $0.25 reclaim level and far from the $1.37 threshold that would mark a shift into a broader bull-market phase.

Whether the base develops the same way as last cycle depends on price reclaiming those levels and on the wider altcoin market providing the liquidity. In the meantime, any Cardano holder still delegated to a retired pool can restore rewards by simply choosing an active one.

Polygon developers now propose a step that has long been considered an absolute taboo in the crypto industry. They put to a vote a plan to rescue Binance and Polymarket money, and this plan is, to say it mildly, radical — zero out the hackers’ wallets at the protocol level. Ongoing cybersecurity crisis shows no signs of stopping, and now the industry is being faced with an uncomfortable choice: save systemic players or protect the inviolability of Web3’s main rule that transactions cannot be reversed. The Polygon PoS hard fork involves seizing 70.49 million POL tokens ($6.5 million at the time of the attack) from the hacker addresses to return them to the victims.

The crisis unfolded at the end of October after two independent hacks. The stolen assets were scattered across five wallets (23.86 million POL was taken from Polymarket, 46.63 million from Binance). Yes, Polygon validators immediately blacklisted the addresses, cutting off the outflow, but this is just an attempt to hold back the dam with bare hands. Manual blocking is a temporary plug, and the authors of the proposal openly admit it.

The hacker is not giving up either and is continuously bombarding the network with transactions carrying wild fees of up to 219,000 POL, counting on automation or a validator with a weakness for easy money to let the operation through for a windfall profit. Things have gone as far as direct attempts to bribe validators with cash, and the hacker simply ignored on-chain negotiations. The developers’ logic is simple: keeping millions in a manual “ban” forever is a dead end that leaves the entire network under constant fire.

No one has access to the hacker’s private keys, so Polygon is changing the consensus rules themselves. Should the hard fork get approval at a certain block, the hackers’ balances will be zeroed out, and an equivalent amount will be mirror-credited to verified Binance and Polymarket wallets — without any token printing.

Polygon Labs is well aware that such an administrative step completely negates the very idea of decentralization.

This plan inevitably triggers a strong sense of the notorious The DAO hard fork of 2016. Back then, to save the young Ethereum ecosystem, developers also had to go through a painful split of the community and ignore the “Code is Law” principle. But Polygon Labs hopes that in their case consensus among validators is already rock-solid, so they are narrowing the framework of the precedent as much as possible, positioning the fork as an exclusively one-time action.

The fate of the millions in POL token is being decided right now in a community vote. The largest validators are already in favor, since both platforms are critically important to Polygon’s survival. If the plan is approved, the software will be released after two weeks of testing, and exchanges and node operators will have to urgently update. Those who refuse to switch to the new code face automatic isolation on the old branch of the blockchain — with no connection to the main network.

#5162. Raw Denim vs. Regular Denim: Which Is Actually Worth Buying?

Here’s what to know about both kinds of jeans.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

I COME FROM the denim era where streetwear juggernauts like FUBU and Rocawear reigned supreme, along with mall favorites like Abercrombie & Fitch and Hollister. I was in my preteens rocking all these clothing brands and you couldn’t tell me their baggy-stacking-at-the-shoe jeans weren’t the flyest on the market. Since I began working as a fashion editor, I’ve practically worn every pair of jeans in the denim universe. Slim, relaxed, stretch, washed, distressed—you name it, I’ve probably tried it. I’ve even tried my hand at denim-making in Japan, the mecca of old-school, high-quality denim, where I produced my own pair of selvedge jeans. Denim is one of those rare items in a guy’s wardrobe that never goes out of style.

And after years of being in the menswear space, I’ve gotten familiar with the nuances that distinguish one kind of denim from the next. Two worth knowing are regular denim and raw denim. Raw denim usually looks darker, stiffer, and more uniform in color, while regular denim has a softer feel and a more broken-in appearance with visible fading or whiskering from factory washing and finishing. Those differences also affect how each pair feels when you first put it on and how it changes over the years. Here’s what to know about both and which one deserves a spot in your rotation.

Regular jeans are usually made by weaving cotton yarn into denim, then cutting fabric into patterns and sewing them together to create the finished garment. These jeans have already gone through washing or finishing treatments to soften the fabric and give them that broken-in look, so you don’t have to spend weeks waiting for them to feel comfortable. If I want to throw on a pair of jeans and get on with my day, this is the kind I’m reaching for. I also like that you can find them in practically every fit and wash, whether you’re after a clean, dark indigo pair or something faded and lived-in. Most everyday options from brands like Levi’s and Wrangler run roughly $40 to $100, while designer and premium styles can cost considerably more. For me, prewashed denim makes the most sense when you want that comfortable feel from the jump. There’s nothing wrong with skipping the break-in period and getting straight to the good part.

I like raw denim because you get to see how jeans change the more you wear them. Unlike prewashed jeans, raw denim typically hasn’t been washed after the dyeing and manufacturing process, so it typically arrives stiff, dark, and pretty rigid. One thing to watch out for, though, is dye transfer. Indigo can rub off onto lighter-colored clothes, shoes, and other materials, including suede. I’ve had this happen before, so I'd be mindful of what you wear with a fresh pair. But that’s part of the appeal for denim enthusiasts. As you wear it, the fabric softens and develops fades and creases based on how you move, sit, and live in your jeans. You’re essentially breaking them in yourself, which makes the finished look feel uniquely yours. Prices can start around $60 to $100 for entry-level options and climb to $150 to $300 or more for premium denim, particularly Japanese-made styles. I’ll admit, the break-in period takes some patience, but if you enjoy watching your jeans evolve over time, raw denim is worth considering.

Raw denim and selvedge denim get lumped together all the time, but they actually refer to different things. Raw denim describes the fabric’s finishing state: It’s typically sold without a post-production wash that softens the fabric or creates a faded look. Selvedge, on the other hand, refers to how the denim is woven, creating a clean, self-finished edge you can often spot by rolling up the cuff. You can have raw selvedge denim, washed selvedge denim, or raw denim that isn’t selvedge at all. Having made my own pair of selvedge jeans in Japan, I’ve seen firsthand how the construction differs. Once you know what to look for, the distinction is pretty easy to spot.

At the end of the day, I don’t think you need to drop $300 on raw denim to dress well. After years of working in menswear, I’ve learned that a higher price tag doesn’t automatically make something the right choice for your wardrobe. I’ve seen guys look just as good in an affordable pair of Levi’s as they do in premium Japanese denim. What matters more is finding comfortable jeans that fit your body and work with the clothes you already own. I’m always going to appreciate the quality craftsmanship behind a great pair of raw denim, but there’s no single right way to wear jeans. I think every guy should have one dependable pair, whether that’s raw or prewashed. But ultimately, like most things in style, it comes down to personal preference—and knowing what works for you.

#5157. South Korea Announces Delay in Crypto Taxation Policy

South Korea announced a delay in the introduction of its cryptocurrency capital gains tax until 2029, extending the tax-free period by two years as authorities plan on strengthening regulatory oversight and connecting data from exchanges with the United States, yna.co.kr reports.

Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il announced the proposal Thursday, acknowledging that the government would be postponing the controversial tax for a fourth time already.

Originally, the policy was scheduled to become active in January 2022: it would impose a 22% tax, local income tax on all cryptocurrency-related gains that exceed 2.5 million won.

While the proposed delay could provide a relief for the South Korean cryptocurrency market and even support the domestic trading activity, it remains a substantial risk factor for both local and overseas investors.

Officials argue that implementing the tax before international information-sharing systems become operational could disadvantage local exchanges and complicate enforcement against overseas trading activity.

Future tax liabilities aren't going to be eliminated, additional time to develop a comprehensive taxation network is more likely to enforce even more limitations on investors in the future, rather than a premature implementation with various legal loopholes.

The government also intends to introduce provisions allowing investors to carry forward cryptocurrency investment losses for up to three years, potentially reducing taxable gains in subsequent periods.

South Korea is also going to establish a separate working group that is going to further refine taxation rules and hopefully simplify reporting requirements for investors, considering the complexity of reporting digital assets transactions and traders on exchanges.

Legislative amendments are expected to reach the National Assembly in 2027.

Authorities reported the continuous coordinating with the Financial Services Commission to accelerate digital assets legislation, providing more transparency and investors protection.

For the industry in general, the proposed extension is more of a transition stage that should improve the competitiveness of the digital assets market, despite introducing stricter tax enforcement. Unfortunately for retail investors, it creates another barrier that might push fresh funds further away from the industry.

#5155. The 8 Best Slip-On Walking Shoes, According to Our Editors

Looking to get out the door quicker? Don’t let laces slip you up.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

SLIDING INTO A pair of slip-on walking shoes might be the easiest thing you’ll do all day. This footwear was built for speed and convenience, making it an accessory that deserves valuable real estate by your door.

Slip-on walking shoes have a rocky history—older versions had a looser fit, raising the risk of instability and friction, especially with higher mileage. But newer designs use no-tie laces, sock liners, pull tabs, and collapsible heels to create a custom fit that rivals what you’ll get with traditional laces.

These shoes are an obvious choice if you have dexterity issues, but they're also just convenient for everyone looking for an easy pair of walking shoes. Slip-on walking shoes also offer more structure than other laceless shoe designs, which has earned them a fanbase with podiatrists. “They are typically a much better option than flip-flops or slides because they provide more stability and keep the foot properly secured,” says Melissa Lockwood, DPM, a podiatrist at Heartland Foot and Ankle Associates in Bloomington, Illinois.

Nicole Graf, DPM, founder of Lexington Podiatry and associate professor at the University of Kentucky, also calls slip-on walking shoes a “huge step up” from flip-flops and slides.

Slip-on walking shoes aren’t for everyone. The fit can still throw some people off, and some simply prefer the tighter feel that laces deliver. But if you want travel-friendly shoes you can toss on in a second, these are a solid choice. As people who value quality, supportive footwear, Men’s Health editors have put in plenty of miles in slip-on walking shoes. The below check all the boxes.

The On Cloud 6 is an excellent example of how good a slip-on shoe can be. You can get in and out of this sneaker with no issue thanks to its wide opening, but the shoe’s elastic “speed” laces and sockliner create a snug fit once you’re in. (Those elastic laces can be adjusted to find your perfect fit.)

The sneaker uses Zero-Gravity CloudTec, which is On’s signature lightweight foam with hollow pods below for a cushioned, yet stable, feel underfoot. (Just be aware that those pods are prone to trapping small pebbles and debris.) A built-in flexible plate, called a Speedboard, helps push you forward with each step. This shoe also comes in a waterproof option, if you’re into rainy strolls. With a wide range of color options and an unobnoxious design, you can pair these with just about anything.

It’s tough to find a quality shoe under $100 right now, let alone one from a big brand. But the Adidas Cloudfoam Cuxxion Sock Shoes have some colorways under $50, making them an ideal choice for budget shoppers who don’t want to mess with laces.

This shoe uses Adidas’ signature Cloudfoam technology at the midsole for a plush, cushioned feel. Its Adiwear outsole is durable and grippy enough for most needs, too. But the real standout in this shoe is its elastic sock upper. It molds to your foot to create a surprisingly snug feel, even for narrow feet. The elastic sock collar supports that secure feel, although it may be too tight for people with wider ankles. The engineered knit upper is highly breathable, lowering the odds you’ll end your walk with sweaty feet. We appreciate the oversized pull tabs in front and back, making the process of getting these on and off seamless.

Feet come in all sizes, making it tough to find a slip-on shoe that works for everyone—and putting adjustable features at a premium. The Nike Pegasus 42 EasyOn has a specialized EasyOn lacing and bungee system up top to help you get the level of tightness you want, before locking it into place. (The lock and bungee combination takes some practice to get right at first.)

The shoe has a collapsible heel that springs back into place once you’re in, making the process of getting these on seamless. It’s also crafted with the same ReactX foam and Air Zoom unit as the standard—and popular—Nike Pegasus 42 running shoe, delivering an energetic feel under your feet. Convenient pull tabs at the heel sit flush against the shoe when they’re not in use, adding to the shoe’s overall sleekness.

Read More: Best Walking Shoes for Men Over 50

Stability shoes are designed to guide your foot with each step and prevent too much inward rolling as you go. But choosing a stability shoe usually means sacrificing a high level of cushioning, since a shoe that feels too plush may not be overly supportive. Hoka’s Skyward Laceless manages to create a stable, locked-in feel while still delivering plenty of the brand’s signature cushioning underfoot.

The Skyward Laceless has a stretchy upper that gently hugs your foot, creating a sock-like feel. The ankle and instep are equally snug, which can be a good or bad thing, depending on your foot size and width. This shoe has plenty of foam below for a slightly bouncy feel, but it still corrects your stride as you go. The integrated tongue pull tab is a nice touch, making for easier entry.

The Under Armour SlipSpeed Mega is packed with features you won’t find in most slip-on walking shoes, creating a versatile, unique sneaker. For starters, this shoe converts from a sneaker design to a recovery slipper with the help of a collapsible heel. (Under Armour refers to this as going from “speed mode” to “slip mode.”)

The shoe skips elastic laces or a sockliner upper in favor of Under Armour’s specialized BOA fit system, a 12-point dial that you can turn to adjust the width across the midfoot. The wide base creates a stable feel, while lots of foam cushioning underfoot delivers a plushness you’ll appreciate. A heads-up: This shoe is slightly heavier than others at 11.7 ounces. That’s a difference you may start to feel on long walks.

After a grueling workout, it feels borderline pampering to slide into the right recovery shoe. The Kane Footwear Active Recovery Shoe is armed with features that should make it a fixture in your gym bag.

This slip-on has strong arch support and a slight rocker shape to help ease pressure on the bottom of your feet as you walk. Internal nodes in the footbed help to promote blood flow and circulation down below, while the shoe’s surprisingly secure design helps prevent slipping. The Active Recovery Shoe is water-resistant with an airy design that allows you to take this in and out of the gym shower without ending up with sopping feet. Heel tabs in back make it simple to get in and out.

Merrell is known for its rugged, outdoor footwear and hiking shoes. While the Merrell Jungle Moc isn’t exactly a hiking shoe, it’s a solid option when you want good traction, whether you’re navigating rocky ground or a slippery surface. The Jungle Moc has been a bestseller for years, with its simple slip-on design and high level of cushioning.

Dual side stretch panels and an exaggerated heel tab make it simple to get in and out of these shoes. The suede upper is breathable, but water-resistant to keep you dry in nearly all conditions. The Jungle Moc has a cushioned EVA midsole for stability and comfort, too. While these shoes are easy to get on, the curved heel makes it harder to slide out—just something to be aware of.

Clogs admittedly aren’t the right style for everyone—some offer less support than sneakers and may slip around more than a standard shoe. But the sleek Crocs Dylan Clog is a solid option for people who want a clog style without some of the common issues that come with it.

The Dylan Clog has a deep heel cup to help lock your foot in, lowering the risk it’ll move around as you step. It’s also made from one piece of Croslite (Crocs’ signature material) to prevent wear and tear over time. This shoe looks like leather thanks to its subtle pebbled texture, but it’s water-resistant and dries quickly when wet. The only major downside is that it’s not very breathable in front. If you’re prone to sweaty toes, this may not be the shoe for you.

Not all shoes are created equal, but the best slip-on walking shoes have all of the supportive features you’ll find in standard lace-up walking shoes. “You mostly get what you pay for in these,” says Richard H. Graves, DPM, a podiatrist at Sol Foot & Ankle Centers in Long Beach, California. He suggests taking a pass at dirt-cheap slip-on walking shoes. “The cheaper ones are not going to provide enough support in the long run, even if they might feel good at first,” Graves says. “There should be enough structure to support your arch and the midsole should be firm and not too flimsy.”

Many high-quality slip-on walking shoes provide similar comfort to regular sneakers. Look for elements like a breathable upper, pull tabs to make them easy to get on and off, and a roomy toe box. Structured heel panels and extra padding in this area help to keep your foot secure, even without standard laces.

Traction for slip-on walking shoes will vary depending on the type of shoe you choose. Most will offer decent traction—meaning, enough so you don’t feel like you’re slipping on wet or damp pavement. But a more rugged shoe like the Merrell Jungle Moc has a grippier sole to help provide extra traction over rockier ground.

Yes, slip-on walking shoes can provide arch support. If this is an important quality for you, look for features like contoured footbeds and a stable midsole. You’ll also want a shoe that fits well and stays put once it’s on to ensure your arch support is consistent. “Make sure that you're not getting them too loose just to make it easier to slide on and off—then you'll be sacrificing support,” Graves says.

To find the best men’s slip-on walking shoes, MH editors tested the most recent and popular pairs on the market, evaluating each for support, comfort, and traction. Because these shoes are designed for walking, not just comfort, durability was also a key factor. To round things out, we consulted three podiatrists for their input on how to evaluate a slip-on walking shoe, along with the value of this style. Based on their advice and our experience, we chose these slip-on walking shoes.

#5154. Bitcoin Mining Giant MARA Sparks Selling Concerns With $133 Million Transfer

Bitcoin mining behemoth MARA Holdings has again raised concerns over possible selling pressure on Bitcoin after it transferred around $133 million worth of BTC to multiple institutional crypto platforms.

According to data from blockchain analytics firm Lookonchain, MARA moved a total of 1,650 BTC (around $132.8 million) to platforms like Galaxy Digital, Copper, and others in the past 12 hours.

The latest transactions, which were first reported on Nov. 5, came a few weeks after a series of massive Bitcoin movements involving the publicly listed mining company.

It seems MARA is once again dumping Bitcoin, referencing recent transfers of massive amounts of BTC to trading platforms and custodians.

Nevertheless, it is possible that the transfers do not actually indicate that MARA has sold BTC.

It's worth noting that platforms like Galaxy Digital and Copper offer different services, including trading and custody, for institutional clients.

So it could be that MARA moved the assets for liquidity, collateral, or other purposes.

It's worth mentioning that the latest BTC movements come after a few similar transactions involving MARA throughout October.

On Oct. 9, MARA moved around 996 BTC ($81.13 million at that time) to a wallet linked to crypto platform Galaxy Digital.

The transaction prompted some speculation about possible BTC selling, though it didn't confirm whether Galaxy Digital actually liquidated the assets or not.

On Oct. 19, Lookonchain again identified some other transactions involving wallets linked to the Bitcoin miner.

As per the analytics firm's data, the wallets linked to the Bitcoin miner sent 1,000 BTC (approximately $82.8 million) to crypto exchanges like Binance.

Towards the end of October, concerns over possible selling increased.

Specifically, on Oct. 27, MARA moved another 1,000 BTC (around $80.19 million) to institutional crypto custody platform BitGo.

The following day, Lookonchain noted another transaction of 1,000 BTC, worth about $80.66 million, to BitGo.

As per its second-quarter financial disclosure, MARA sold around 23,093 BTC for $1.6 billion in the first half of 2026.

In the second quarter alone, MARA sold 2,213 BTC at an average price of $73,078.

Meanwhile, MARA has also made it clear that it is no longer interested in holding all the Bitcoin it mines.

#5152. Binance Revokes API Keys, Security Issue Found at SignalPlus

Binance has revoked all API keys associated with SignalPlus after the digital asset trading infrastructure provider identified a potential security vulnerability, prompting the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange to take measures to protect users, according to the latest report on the Binance's official Square feed.

The exchange confirmed Thursday that the decision was intended to prevent possible unauthorized access through connections established between Binance accounts and SignalPlus. Binance emphasized that its internal systems had not been compromised and that customer funds remained safe.

For now, the reason or the nature of the incident remains unclear. Both companies have yet to disclose how serious the potential vulnerability is or how many users may be affected. It is still unclear whether the attackers gained access to customer accounts or if the incident caused any financial losses.

The development underscores the security challenges associated with third-party infrastructure in cryptocurrency markets, where trading platforms increasingly depend on external applications for execution, analytics and automation.

Binance's security documentation advises users to revoke potentially compromised credentials immediately and restrict API permissions to necessary functions.

For affected SignalPlus users, restoring automated trading functionality may require generating new credentials once the integration is deemed secure.

SignalPlus provides trading infrastructure and analytical tools for cryptocurrency derivatives markets, allowing traders to manage positions and execute strategies across exchanges through API integrations.

These connections enable third-party applications to interact with exchange accounts without requiring users to transfer their assets off-platform. However, depending on the permissions granted, compromised API credentials can potentially expose accounts to unauthorized trading activity.

Binance has effectively severed existing integrations between its platform and SignalPlus. The measure could potentially disrupt automated trading strategies that rely on those connections.

According to one of the architects of the XRP Ledger, now Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz, his retirement from active development almost a year ago came at the right time. "I picked a great time to retire!", said Schwartz, reacting to the latest report from OpenAI researchers, which touches on testing a new cyber model. Just one autonomous run and the AI completely changed the familiar standards of network security, OpenAI researcher Eric Wallace confirms.

The report shows how OpenAI's pipeline works. First thing to understand, it's a fully complete cycle: the system independently finds a potential bug, verifies it, writes a working exploit to confirm it and automatically releases a patch. This was tested on the Linux kernel, the core software that runs most of the planet's servers (including OpenAI's own compute clusters).

The Web3 sphere is one where open-source code is the foundation of blockchain security, so this development is a challenge to say the least. If AI finds zero-day vulnerabilities in a matter of hours, manual code auditing by humans becomes useless.

Yes, Schwartz stepped down from the post of Ripple CTO into honorary retirement last November, but he hasn't abandoned his terminal. Just recently he showed monitoring charts of his personal server hub on the XRP Ledger network. There, a node is running under colossal load: it maintains more than 550 active connections (peers), shows latency of around 200ms and processes about 110,000 incoming messages per second.

Besides, Schwartz continues personal work on the network's internal architectural problems. In a discussion with active validators, Schwartz detailed a transaction queue bug that caused the local load metric on his server to jump to 540, triggering fee spikes within the ledger.

Schwartz picked the "right time" to step back from Ripple, but he's clearly not out of the game.

#5149. Binance Hack Recovery Hits 98%, Proof of Reserves Expands to 44 Tokens

Home » Crypto Market News » Binance Hack Recovery Hits 98%, Proof of Reserves Expands to 44 Tokens

Binance is restoring withdrawals for 62 tokens while expanding zero-knowledge reserve checks after historic breach.

Binance reported major progress in its recovery efforts following the October 29 historic hot wallet breach.

The crypto exchange said that its hack recovery has reached about 98% of affected users’ asset value following the $6.3 billion hack. The exchange is also reopening withdrawals for 62 tokens and expanding its zero-knowledge Proof-of-Reserves (PoR) coverage.

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance published its eighth recovery update on November 5, confirming that it has successfully replenished approximately 98% of the user asset value affected by the October 29 hack.

The exchange also noted that it will gradually restore withdrawals for 69 network-asset pairs covering 62 tokens across six blockchains starting at 04:00 UTC on November 5.

Ethereum accounts for 36 assets, followed by BNB Chain (24), Base (4), TRON (3), Polygon (1), and Sui (1).

Binance said it prioritized assets based on user demand over the past week, with each withdrawal pair subject to security and readiness checks. It also warned that some tokens may not be immediately available, and high traffic could cause processing delays.

Binance’s reported replenishment progress advanced from 90% on October 31 to 95% on November 1, reaching 98% in the November 4 report.

The exchange said it would cover all losses using corporate funds, including its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), Futures Insurance Fund and corporate treasury reserves, with no losses passed on to retail customers.

The remaining 2% consists of less liquid tokens that Binance is sourcing through open markets and over-the-counter (OTC) deals. The exchange said acquiring them could take longer due to limited liquidity, making large purchases more likely to cause price slippage and volatility.

Binance also expanded its Proof of Reserves coverage from 10 to 44 tokens, introducing zero-knowledge verification, which allows users to confirm their balances are backed at least 1:1.

The exchange said generating the cryptographic proofs would take an estimated 50 to 60 hours. Once complete, holders of the covered assets will be able to verify that Binance holds reserves equal to at least 100% of its customer liabilities.

Initial reports and blockchain analytics firms estimated that attackers stole about $6.3 billion in digital assets across 10 blockchains during an attack that lasted roughly 20 minutes.

Tether, Circle and other major stablecoin issuers froze an estimated $2.65 billion to $3 billion in stolen assets, or about 42% of the total funds drained, according to compliance and analytics reports. The remaining assets, including 18,270 BTC and more than 420,000 ETH, remain largely untouched in identified hacker wallets.

Findings released by the FBI attributed the breach to TraderTraitor, a hacking group linked to North Korea.

Binance’s replenishment and expanded PoR address the key question after a major exchange breach: whether user funds are fully backed. The outcome could influence how other exchanges approach reserve transparency.

#5148. Zcash targets 67% shorter block times – Can ZEC overcome funding uncertainty?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Zcash [ZEC] is preparing a major network upgrade that will reduce block time. The network upgrade (NU7) is designed to shorten the time it takes for blocks to be processed.

Set to be implemented on the 6th of November, this new system will enable Zcash to decrease block processing times by approximately 67%, from 75 seconds to 25 seconds.

Simply, the direct result of this change will likely be the ability for users to finalize transactions significantly faster than before. In addition, it will enable the network to process more total activity, all without altering the amount of ZEC that is added to circulation each day.

Notably, there are two other aspects of the upgrade in need of attention. First, the Sprout pool will no longer exist. Second, 60% of every transaction fee collected by the network will now go into a deferred reserve.

However, how successful these upgrades are in creating the desired effect will depend on whether the faster confirmation rates create increased adoption on-chain.

Although NU7 improves the way Zcash’s network operates, the Zcash funding model faces a separate challenge.

Who gets to control the future funding for development was a subject of debate for weeks prior to the 3rd of November. This was when Zcash Community Grants announced that it had withdrawn its proposal to direct about 98,000 ZEC into future miner rewards.

Notably, that amount represented about half of its entire treasury.

The proposal would have drawn 36,200 ZEC from ZCG’s 91,500-ZEC treasury, with the remainder coming from reduced future allocations through 2028. However, its withdrawal leaves the original funding structure intact.

As such, ZCG will continue receiving 8% of newly issued ZEC, equivalent to roughly 144 ZEC daily. Miners retain 80%, while 12% enters the coinholder-controlled lockbox.

Although withdrawing the proposal leaves current distributions intact, alternative proposals continue to leave long-term funding for development uncertain.

Beyond governance uncertainty, Zcash’s institutional demand also shows signs of weakening, although recent flows suggest a possible shift. ZEC spot ETFs recorded three consecutive days of withdrawals, with weekly net outflows reaching $7.21 million.

However, the 4th of November saw a $3.43 million inflow into ZEC spot ETFs, ending the streak of net outflows. The inflow increased total cumulative net inflows to $217.73 million and net assets to $756.83 million. Volume also hit $59.45 million.

While there was an increase in net inflows recently, recent outflows indicate that institutions become more cautious. Additionally, while ETFs still hold 3.43% of outstanding circulation of ZEC, institutions do maintain a significant presence in spite of decreased demand.

XRP just formed a new short-term golden cross versus Bitcoin, and the market is weighing whether the technical signal can underpin more upside.

A golden cross is when a shorter-term moving average crosses above a longer-term moving average. In this case, the 50 MA crossing above the 200 MA.

This signal appearing on the XRP/BTC 3-hour chart might suggest improving momentum and a possible short-term trend change.

The development is especially important for XRP, since it could propel renewed strength against Bitcoin. On a 24-hour basis, XRP is outperforming Bitcoin in percentage gains, up 2.19% while Bitcoin was up 1.74% in the same timeframe. However, a golden cross is not a guarantee of sustained upside, and traders will be watching whether price action confirms the signal.

In a recent X post, Ali, a crypto analyst, pointed to a spike in XRP exchange outflows. He said that around 01:00 UTC today, about 13.24 million XRP were withdrawn from exchanges, potentially reducing the immediate supply for sale.

#5146. Zcash (ZEC) Co-Founder Issues Warning on AI Security Threat

Zcash co-founder and computer scientist Eli Ben-Sasson has issued a crucial warning about crypto security amid recent hacker attacks on crypto wallets.

In his latest post on X, Ben-Sasson wrote that the crypto industry faces a key threat besides quantum computers. In particular, he pointed to the growing capabilities of AI as a tool for cybersecurity attacks.

The reason is that today, more than ever before, we rely on cryptography.

"Your crypto keys, your online life, any app that holds something important to you — it's all secured by cryptography," he wrote.

According to Ben-Sasson, the growing power of AI tools puts more pressure on wallet cryptography. This threat is more likely to become an issue before quantum computers pose a significant threat.

"This quick rise in cybersecurity attacks is not going to slow down, not with AI becoming so powerful," Ben-Sasson wrote.

The Zcash co-founder also pointed out the need for stronger cryptographic standards. He specifically highlighted hash-based methods such as ZK-STARKs.

The discussion comes weeks after the infamous Binance hack. The incident resulted in around $6.3 billion in losses from the exchange's hot wallets.

Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals while investigating the breach. The exchange has since reported recovering around 95% of the affected assets.

AI hacker attacks have been on the rise in 2026. According to Google Threat Intelligence statistics, the monthly number of disclosed software vulnerabilities has nearly doubled over the past year.

This means that AI has already become a powerful scanner for potential system weaknesses.

For instance, Casa CSO Jameson Lopp pointed out that attackers can already use AI to automate the search for conventional software bugs and weaknesses in wallet firmware.

In other words, the discussion should be focused on more specific security vulnerabilities in existing software rather than a hypothetical future AI threat.

#5145. Weekend stock tokens predict Monday open, but guessing up scores 55%

Bitquery’s pre-futures weekend test found no clear directional edge, while Nasdaq’s proposed weekday expansion remains conditional.

Stock tokens kept trading through weekends, but their prices did not reliably guide the next stock-market open in a new study of 121 stocks.

Blockchain data provider Bitquery's Nov. 3 analysis found that Sunday token moves measured before equity-index futures reopened correctly called 54% of qualifying openings, so simply predicting that every stock would open higher scored 55%.

More hours can give investors another opportunity to transact, but they do not show that the resulting prices predict the next opening better.

Bitquery followed 17 weekends beginning July 10 through Oct. 30, with the final stock opening on Nov. 2. It recorded 791 stock-opening observations across those stocks, and its direction test kept the 533 openings that moved at least 0.5% from Friday's close.

Token moves pointed the right way on 286 of those observations, compared with 291 correct calls for always predicting a rise. Because more openings rose than fell, a 50% coin-toss benchmark alone would flatter the tokens' result.

The study also used balanced accuracy, which averages success on rises and falls. The tokens scored 53%, with a reported 95% interval of 44% to 62%.

Across all 791 observations, including smaller moves, the median error was 1.2% using token moves versus 0.9% assuming the stock opened at Friday's close. Bitquery put the excess error at 0.3%, with a 95% range of 0.2% to 0.5%.

Bitquery's study asks different questions about direction and forecast size. The later Sunday reading also changes the information and the sample.

The main direction test ends just before futures reopen. It filters on the stock's opening move.

The later check follows futures reopening and changes both liquidity and movement filters.

Trading access and useful forecasting information remain separate claims.

Vendor research, not independent raw-data replication. No futures-price benchmark or cost-adjusted strategy. The later cutoff, volume floor and movement filter change together.

Reported study figures only. Main test: 17 weekends beginning July 10–October 30, openings through November 2. Direction filters stock moves below 0.5%; size uses all 791 observations. Panel intervals are reported 95% ranges. Point and interval geometry maps linearly onto the same 40%–70% balanced-accuracy scale; this is an interval plot, not a zero-based bar chart.

Vendor research, not independent raw-data replication. No futures-price benchmark or cost-adjusted strategy. The later cutoff, volume floor and movement filter change together.

The main test read token prices just before 6 p.m. Sunday ET, the futures reopening cutoff used by Bitquery. That timing is important because a later token price could incorporate information already available from equity-index futures.

A separate check using prices just before 8 p.m. returned 59% balanced accuracy, with a 95% range of 53% to 65%, across 220 openings. But it also raised the weekend-volume threshold to $1 million and changed the movement filter.

Listings needed at least $10,000 of weekend trading and a trade in the hour before each cutoff. The study excluded openings affected by stock splits or ex-dividend dates and crypto-sensitive stocks such as Strategy and Coinbase, then combined issuers using weekend-volume weights.

Earlier perpetual-market research reported improved forecasts from final weekend prices in a different sample. Different instruments, liquidity filters and observation times prevent that result from serving as a direct rebuttal to this test.

Nasdaq's Oct. 30 update described Dec. 6 as the expected transition to 23-hour, five-day trading, subject to clearing and market-data infrastructure being ready. Its related market-data proposals also remain subject to regulatory approval.

Its member implementation notice describes an added 9 p.m. to 4 a.m. ET session requiring new member ports.

If the rollout proceeds, wider conventional weekday hours would narrow one stock-token advantage for investors whose brokers and jurisdictions permit both routes. Weekend trading and the ability to hold tokens in a blockchain wallet remain separate benefits to assess.

For example, Kraken's xStocks disclosure excludes the US, Canada, UK and Australia, permits compatible-wallet withdrawals and says holders lack ownership and voting rights in the underlying shares.

The next useful evidence would hold timing and eligibility constant, compare against available market benchmarks, and measure executable results after costs. Until then, an available weekend price should not be mistaken for a demonstrated forecasting advantage.

Trump-linked tokens suffered sharp losses while XRP and Bitcoin rallied, according to Money Maker a.k.a Avi Lev, a crypto-market commentator who argues that scrutiny of the president’s business interests need not derail broader crypto legislation.

Avi Lev’s central claim: bipartisan support for digital assets could matter more than the fortunes of individual political ventures.

The video frames these moves around the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, citing Stand With Crypto’s tally of 245 elected pro-crypto candidates.

However, the transcript does not establish its publication date or independently substantiate those election results, and it gives conflicting percentages for pro-crypto winners.

Avi Lev reports declines of roughly 19% for the TRUMP token, 14% for MELANIA and 4% for WLFI. Trump Media shares reportedly fell about 24% in the session discussed, with the commentator noting that earnings also contributed to the pressure.

The YouTube video clip connects those losses to anticipated Democratic investigations into Trump’s crypto ventures and other business dealings. That explanation is the host’s interpretation, rather than a demonstrated cause of the price moves.

XRP, meanwhile, was quoted near $1.31 after a broader crypto rally. Bitcoin traded around $79,481 before settling into a tighter consolidation range alongside Ethereum; XRP and Solana showed wider price swings, according to the chart commentary.

Avi Lev quotes Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse describing a “new Congress with the same mission,” pointing to support for crypto on both sides of the aisle. The video also cites reporting that House Democrats want to revive their preferred CLARITY Act provisions within broader market-structure legislation.

#5143. French bank resumes transfers after $133 million attack but leaves crypto loss unconfirmed

Arkéa says attackers used its own account through a provider's platform, while a separate $108.8 million USDC trail leaves the bank-to-crypto link unproven.

French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said almost all operations had resumed on Nov. 4 after an attack enabled fraudulent crypto transactions from its own account, delaying some customer transfers.

In a later clarification, the bank said attackers reached it through a service provider's platform and sent money to other banks. Those transactions may then have enabled conversion into cryptocurrency through specialized platforms.

Arkéa did not confirm that conversion or connect its transfers to specific crypto wallets.

The bank denied that the attack entered through Fortuneo, its online banking subsidiary, and said it did not use customer accounts. It described the incident as contained and said customers' holdings were unaffected.

Arkéa declined to confirm whether €118 million ($133 million) had been stolen and validated only their order of magnitude. It said some funds had been blocked and further recovery efforts were underway, making a definitive financial amount premature.

The amount involved in fraudulent transactions is not necessarily the bank's final loss once blocked funds and recoveries are accounted for. Arkéa said the sums would not threaten its financial strength.

Its initial statement described precautionary transaction suspensions and a gradual restart after checks and stronger security measures. The later update said almost all operations had resumed during the morning.

Arkéa said it was working with judicial and police authorities to determine the attack's origin and method.

Separately, blockchain analytics firm Bitquery reported tracing $108.8 million in USDC withdrawals from wallets it labels as belonging to Kraken, Crypto.com and OKX to 15 addresses on Nov. 1 and 2. The withdrawals ran from 12:25 UTC on Nov. 1 to 09:09 UTC the next day, roughly 21 hours.

Bitquery said it cannot see bank transfers or exchange accounts, so the transactions cannot independently establish the alleged route from Arkéa into crypto or identify the owners of the receiving accounts.

#5142. Hong Kong forces crypto providers to track customer trades

Hong Kong passed its crypto tax-reporting bill, putting provider data collection in 2027 before CARF exchanges in 2028.

Hong Kong's Legislative Council passed a crypto tax-information reporting bill on Nov. 4, requiring covered providers to begin collecting information in 2027 before the Inland Revenue Department starts exchanging it with partner jurisdictions in 2028.

The department's implementation background specifies Jan. 1, 2027, for the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). Providers collect and report information to the tax authority, and the department conducts the international exchanges.

The first collection year comes before the cross-border sharing date for covered firms.

CARF establishes due diligence and annual reporting requirements for crypto-asset service providers. It concerns tax transparency, with providers gathering information that tax authorities can use, rather than setting an individual user's tax bill.

The bill also implements the amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS) for financial account information. The government says that the revised standard takes effect in 2028, with exchanges starting in 2029. Its schedule is separate from CARF's 2027 collection and 2028 exchange timetable.

One bill, two reporting calendars. Follow the information from covered providers to tax authorities.

Providers identify reportable users, collect the required information and report annually to the tax authority.

The Inland Revenue Department exchanges CARF information with partner jurisdictions; providers do not conduct that cross-border step.

Covered providers collect CARF information in 2027. The tax department begins international exchanges in 2028.

Announced future schedules, not exact exchange or domestic filing dates. Obligations depend on provider scope.

Year-aligned schedule and a selectable information-route diagram built from the official passage announcement and IRD background. No elapsed-time or filing-deadline calculation is implied.

Announced future schedules, not exact exchange or domestic filing dates. Obligations depend on provider scope.

In December 2024, Hong Kong intended to complete legislative amendments by 2026 and begin crypto-information exchanges in 2028. The Nov. 4 vote marks the legislative milestone ahead of the collection year.

In its CARF explanation, the Inland Revenue Department describes reporting providers as businesses carrying out customer exchanges between crypto-assets and fiat currencies, or between crypto-assets.

These include businesses acting as counterparties or intermediaries and those operating trading platforms. Obligations depend on the provider's connection to a jurisdiction under the framework's nexus rules.

The department describes reportable users, and relevant controlling persons of entity users, by tax residence in reportable jurisdictions. A provider must identify the relevant users or controlling persons before it can prepare information for the annual reporting process described by the department.

Its explanation lists identifying details, tax-residence information, and aggregated transaction information among the required data. That scope is key when assessing a provider's obligations and which customers' information is reportable.

Hong Kong says exchanges will be reciprocal and subject to confidentiality and security safeguards. The Inland Revenue Department will issue guidance and has established a dedicated team to provide technical support and answer industry inquiries.

The department also says it will develop a CARF reporting portal and publish the data schema that defines the reporting format, with further details to follow. Those materials will set out more of the reporting process for providers preparing to collect the required data in 2027.

Glassnode's end-October profitability reset and BlockchainCenter's neutral November 4 breadth reading leave a broad altcoin recovery unconfirmed.

Profit-taking among recent altcoin holders had given way to loss-taking by end-October, according to Glassnode, while fewer than half of the major coins in a separate market index were beating Bitcoin over 90 days.

In its Nov. 4 report, the on-chain analytics firm said short-term holders were spending at a profit in about 12% of its more than 300 tracked tokens by end-October, compared with about 80% in late September.

Separately, BlockchainCenter's Nov. 4 snapshot put its 90-day Altcoin Season Index at 41, meaning fewer than half of its eligible major coins had beaten Bitcoin over that window.

Glassnode uses short-term-holder spent output profit ratio (STH-SOPR) to measure whether those holders sell at a profit or a loss.

A reading above 1 indicates profitable spending, while below 1 indicates loss-making spending. By end-October, the firm said, typical tracked tokens' short-term holders were selling at a small loss.

STH supply in profit is shown as a percentage, and Bitcoin price is shown in thousands of US dollars, so a price value of 100 represents $100,000.

Source: Glassnode chart supplied by the article

The 12% figure counts tokens whose short-term holders sold at a profit.

The site calls it altcoin season when 75% of that universe outperforms Bitcoin, and the Nov. 4 reading shows 41, sitting inside that neutral band.

A token can gain in dollar terms and still trail Bitcoin if Bitcoin rises faster. Similarly, loss-making spending among recent holders can coexist with a stronger relative return measured over a longer window.

Profitable short-term-holder spending contracted across Glassnode's tracked tokens. BlockchainCenter's separate November 4 breadth reading was neutral.

#5139. Matt Corallo Flags Critical Linux Kernel Flaw; Lightning Labs Ships LND Mitigation

Bitcoin Core and Lightning developer Matt Corallo highlighted a severe Linux kernel vulnerability on October 30, criticizing Ubuntu’s delayed response to what he called “the most critical Linux vuln ever.” The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, affects the kernel’s IPv4 TCP handshake code with a CVSS severity score of 9.8. Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team later showed it could be turned into a remote root exploit against systems exposing a Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener.

Peter Todd echoed the warning the same day, advising anyone running LND on Linux with open ports to shut their Bitcoin Lightning nodes down until the kernel was patched or otherwise mitigated. The demonstrated exploit path relies on an MPTCP listener—something Go 1.24 and later enable by default. Because LND is written in Go, recent versions were listening with MPTCP on their peer, gRPC, and REST ports whenever the kernel had the feature enabled.

Lightning Labs responded the same day with emergency releases: lnd v0.21.6-beta and the backport v0.20.7-beta. Both disable MPTCP listeners by default, closing the demonstrated exploit path through LND. The project described the change as a mitigation, not a fix, and noted that only a patched kernel fully resolves the underlying issue. Other services on the same machine remain exposed until MPTCP is disabled host-wide or the kernel is updated. Olaoluwa Osuntokun and the official Lightning Labs account both recommended the update.

Security researcher Marcus Hutchins later reported internet-wide scanning activity consistent with threat actors looking for exposed systems. His scans found roughly 2.1 million servers reachable over MPTCP on port 443. International Cyber Digest amplified the finding on November 4, noting the scanning and Ubuntu’s slower patch timeline.

Canonical has since made fixed kernels available in the opt-in, proposed pocket for Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04, but they have not yet reached the regular updates channel. Red Hat shipped fixes for RHEL 8/9/10 on November 1; Debian, Amazon Linux, and others had already released patches earlier.

UmbrelOS 2.0.1 included the kernel fix on November 1st for x86 devices and applied a traffic-blocking mitigation on Raspberry Pi, where a fixed kernel was not yet available. No confirmed in-the-wild exploitation has been reported, and the vulnerability has not been added to CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Anthropic’s remote-root demonstration remains unpublished.

The practical exposure is highest on internet-facing servers. Home desktop systems behind typical NAT and firewalls, without public TCP listeners, are far less affected. For Lightning operators on Linux, the LND releases remove the specific MPTCP listener path the public exploit used, but the broader kernel bug remains until a patched kernel is installed.

#5138. Influencers Are Doing ‘Olive Oil Shots.’ We Asked 4 Experts If That’s a Good Idea—and They All Basically Said the Same Thing.

The truth about the supposed health practice—revealed.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

SO OLIVE OIL shots are a thing again. Remember in the mid- to late-2010s, when people were knocking back all manner of liquids, including apple cider vinegar, juiced ginger, pulverized turmeric, and extra virgin olive oil? Well, social media influencers have brought back at least the last one, with Bryan Johnson doing “evo” shots and Steven Gundry, MD, recommending a daily dose of the stuff. (Also, both those guys sell their own olive oil. Just saying.)

The supposed benefits of shooting olive range from the more generalized “more energy” to more specific ones, like protecting your cardiovascular system from disease.

Influencers usually back up these claims by citing scientific research on the benefits of adding olive oil to your daily diet. But do the benefits extend to doing shots of olive oil?

“Olive oil is great for heart health and contains beneficial polyphenols, but you don't need to take it as a shot. You get the same benefits by just including it in your meals, and it's generally much more enjoyable that way. But if you want to take it as a shot, there's no harm in that. It's just not superior to including olive oil in your diet in regular ways. You know, with food.”

“I'm a fan of California Olive Ranch 100% California Extra Virgin Olive Oil For Everyday. It's high quality, reasonably affordable (for evoo), and widely available. I use it to saute veggies, roast tubers and veggies, and drizzle on various things.”

“I'm a bigger fan of eating a few shots of olive oil with sauteed veggies or I pour it on my food. But a shot is fine I guess. People like to do it in the longevity scene to invoke ancient Greeks doing shots of ‘liquid gold.’”

“I am an affiliate of the Fresh Pressed Olive Oil Club, which I reallly love. I've not had lots of fancy, fresh olive oils from around the world before and now I have. I like seeing and tasting the diversity. I use a 1-liter glass bottle of EVOO, usually Braggs or Whole Food Organic. I try to go through two to three of these a month for our house of four.”

“I wouldn’t suggest shots of olive oil for any reason. All that’s happening here is that you’re adding a concentrated source of calories and fat to your diet. There are no documented benefits of doing this for the average person, and it can cause weight gain if the oil shots are taken in addition to someone’s current diet. This can ultimately cause health problems.”

“I don’t really have a fave oil. I use brands that have a seal of origin in them to ensure their purity.”

“While olive oil is full of beneficial compounds that may support heart health and longevity, shooting it isn't necessary. Heating olive oil may degrade some beneficial polyphenols, but using it as a salad dressing, sauce, or finishing oil for roasted veggies provides the same benefits, plus enhanced absorption of fat-soluble vitamins and carotenoids.”

“Extra-virgin olive oil can have such a range of flavors. I love San Giuliano Coastal Harvest Olive Oil. It's cold-pressed, which helps preserve more nutrients and polyphenols, and has a really nice, peppery flavor. While I don't take shots of it, I regularly use it in dressings and over veggies.”

#5136. Bitcoin and gold surge after US elections, but $378 million short squeeze casts doubt on debasement trade

Bitcoin’s rally alongside gold revived debasement fears as investors weigh ETF outflows, short covering, and key price levels.

Bitcoin's rally above $81,000 alongside gold has revived speculation that investors are seeking protection against the weakening US dollar.

The largest cryptocurrency rebounded from about $75,600 on Nov. 4, while gold futures surged 3.4% to $4,061.10, their biggest daily gain in three months. The dollar also weakened as investors digested the Democrats' sweeping victory in the US midterm elections.

The simultaneous gains revived talks of “the debasement trade,” a strategy in which investors buy scarce assets such as Bitcoin and gold to protect their wealth against currency depreciation and mounting government debt.

However, broader financial markets told a more complicated story. The S&P 500 jumped 1.6%, the Dow gained 3%, and Treasury yields declined as investors welcomed the prospect of reduced political uncertainty and constraints on President Donald Trump's fiscal agenda.

Those developments suggest Bitcoin's recovery could have more to do with improving market sentiment than a fundamental shift in how investors view the dollar.

The argument that Bitcoin is increasingly behaving like gold has gained traction among institutional investors in recent months.

In August, Grayscale reported that Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with gold had climbed above 0.50 from almost zero earlier in the year. Its correlation with the Nasdaq-100, meanwhile, declined from more than 0.60 to approximately 0.33.

Bitwise subsequently found that Bitcoin's relationship with gold had reached its strongest level since 2020, when extraordinary fiscal and monetary stimulus heightened concerns about the purchasing power of traditional currencies.

Those concerns have a substantial economic foundation. The Congressional Budget Office projects that the US federal deficit will reach $1.9 trillion in 2026 before expanding to $3.1 trillion by 2036, with publicly held debt rising to 120% of GDP.

Yet Wednesday's market reaction offered another explanation for why Bitcoin and gold moved together.

Values digitized from TradingView charts for Nov. 4, 2026, rebased to 0% at 01:00 UTC-3.

Source: TradingView: Binance BTCUSDT, 1-hour · TradingView: TVC Gold, 1-hour

The 10-year Treasury yield declined from approximately 4.95% to 4.89%, while market expectations for inflation over the next year fell from about 2.4% to 2.1%.
